item.description: Francis Lawrence has a lot on his plate following the release of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping . The director, who has helmed five of six Hunger Games movies, is currently juggling a BioShock film , a possible sequel to 2005's Constantine , and an adaptation of the critically acclaimed novel Red Rising . item.title: Michigan no longer having a ‘Beat Ohio’ practice period shows Kyle Whittingham’s out of touch
item.description: EUGENE, OREGON - NOVEMBER 14: Head Coach Kyle Whittingham of the Michigan Wolverines runs off the field at halftime during the game against the Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Ali Gradischer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Michigan was coming off a 2-4 2020 season, the worst of the Jim Harbaugh era. Changes needed to be made, and Harbaugh made many. “Do it or die trying” was Harbaugh’s mantra about beating Ohio State and all of Michigan’s opponents. Another huge change Harbaugh made was changing the 9-on-7 practice period. “It means everything to us; we got the music going, we got the energy going,” former Michigan linebacker Josh Ross said in 2021 . “It’s exciting; we do it every single week.” “We’re blasting music, smelling salts, everything. It’s a pretty physical period,” former Michigan offensive lineman Trevor Keegan said in 2021. “We love it!” After Harbaugh introduced the ‘Beat Ohio’ practice period, Michigan went on to win three consecutive Big Ten Championships, culminating in a national championship win in January of 2024. Despite the successes Michigan had with a portion of practice called ‘Beat Ohio’, Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham and his staff decided to do away with that name. “We don’t call it the ‘Beat Ohio’ practice period, but we’ve definitely spent time on it,” Whittingham told the media on Monday. “Meeting time, on the field time. Obviously, the signage in the building. It’s present every single day of the year. That’s something that does not change and will continue to be emphasized.” Kyle Whittingham says there is no more "Beat Ohio" practice period, but Michigan has devoted time all year to preparing for the Buckeyes pic.twitter.com/dxGeYOStrt — Clayton Sayfie (@CSayf23) November 23, 2026 Whittingham said people would have to be living in a cave to not understand the importance of the Michigan-Ohio State rivalry, yet he made a change that strips the importance of the rivalry a bit. Whittingham called it the biggest rivalry in all of sports, yet got rid of the ‘Beat Ohio’ period of practice, which is known to be the most physical and tenacious. It seems like a counterintuitive decision. Whittingham already lost to another huge rival, Michigan State, and his comments leading up to that matchup weren’t inspiring either. Whittingham gave MSU bulletin board material, calling it the “Super Bowl, particularly for them” while referring to Michigan State as Michigan’s “second-biggest rival.” The 16-6 loss to Michigan State meant Michigan had to surrender the Paul Bunyan Trophy to Michigan State, which was just one of two rivalry trophies they lost this season. Michigan also surrendered the Little Brown Jug to Minnesota after losing to the Golden Gophers in Minneapolis for the first time since 1977. item.title: You Need to Watch GTA 6’s Telenovela Immediately
item.description: There is a ton of stuff to do in Grand Theft Auto 6 . You can rob jewelry stores and steal exotic supercars. You can go scuba diving and hunt for pirate treasure. On the other end of the spectrum, you can trawl yard sales and vintage stores to expand your in-game collection of novelty T-shirts . In addition to a comprehensive variety of radio stations and podcasts, there are also three basic TV channels to choose from: Visit Leonida, Megamundo, and Weazel. The Spanish-language Megamundo — a parody of the real-world Telemundo — is the best of the bunch, and that's all down to one show that sunk its claws into me the second I tuned in: El Destino Extiende Sus Alas , which translates to "destiny spreads its wings."

item.title: How to watch Louisiana football vs Georgia State in Week 13, plus score prediction
item.description: Louisiana football may be a bit banged up but its feeling good after snagging its eighth win of the 2026 season. In Week 12 the Ragin’ Cajuns (8-3, 5-2 SBC) took down Coastal Carolina 38-24 to complete the year a perfect 6-0 at home. Now the Cajuns leave the comforts of Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium to close out the year against Georgia State . It was dual-threat quarterback Lunch Winfield carrying the load offensively in the previous contest. Defensively, UL took most of its bumps and bruises with a handful of linebackers out with injuries entering Week 13. Winfield and the rest of its offensive weapons will need another strong outing to help carry the load for a beat up defense. Stepping up in the linebacker core amid the injuries is sophomore Micah Johnson. Listed at 6-foot and 232 pounds, Johnson has been a ball magnet, recording up to a team-high five fumble recoveries so far this year. The Panthers (5-6, 2-5) are not only looking for a pick me up, but haunting momentum for UL. GSU is on a two-game losing streak, falling to Marshall and Georgia Southern. The Cajuns will look to neutralize the Panthers’ two-man quarterback and running back duo as they aim to be fifth team in UL history to win 10 games in a season. What time is Louisiana football vs Georgia State ? Louisiana football kicks off against Georgia State at 1 p.m. CT, Saturday, Nov. 28, inside Center Parc Credit Union Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. Louisiana football vs Georgia State TV Channel Louisiana football vs Georgia State in Week 13 of the 2026 college football season will stream on ESPN+, where you can stream here . Last time out the Panthers lost a heartbreaker on the road against Marshall, 28-27. Putting a huge chip on their shoulder as they look to close out the year with some momentun on their side. With the Cajuns defense banged up, that could open the path for GSU's quarterback Ayden Pereira, who threw for three touchdowns last week. Winfield will have another big task on his shoulders this week and will need much more help from the run game this week if the Cajuns want to snag win No. 9 this season. The football Gods might be in favor for the underdog at home this week. item.title: 2027 Willie McCovey Memorial Community Prospect List No. 12
item.description: PHOENIX, AZ - JUNE 24: Carson Bolemon #18 poses for a photo during the 2026 Draft Combine at Arizona Grand Resort Phoenix on Wednesday, June 24, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Aryanna Frank/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images We’re a quarter of the way through the 2027 Willie McCovey Memorial Community Prospect List! Our goal is to rank the top 44 prospects in the San Francisco Giants organization, and we’ve officially hit the 25% mark! Rounding out the first quarter is one of the many new players to the system who is on the list: left-handed pitcher Carson Bolemon, who makes his CPL debut as the No. 11 prospect in the system. The Giants drafted Bolemon with the 29th pick in July’s draft out of Southside Christian School in South Carolina. While he’s a little old for a prep player (he’ll turn 20 in April), he’s extremely experienced, as he not only starred in high school (where he threw a 19-strikeout no-hitter in the state championship game), but was also the ace of the 18-and-under Team USA squad that won the World Cup in 2025. Depending on how you like to view things, it’s either good or bad news that Bolemon was available to the Giants at No. 29, since he entered the season as the consensus top pitcher in the draft. Seen through an optimistic lens, the Giants were able to capitalize on a mildly-down year and get the pre-season top-ranked pitcher … as well as the post-season top-ranked pitcher, Jackson Flora. Seen through a more pessimistic lens, the Giants drafted a player who has already started moving downwards, as he was the ninth pitcher off the board in July, after being projected to be the first pitcher off the board a year ago. Bolemon, who is a well-built 6’4, and who famously didn’t give up a single earned run his junior year, has a fastball that’s been a little inconsistent in terms of velocity, but that has good movement that should allow it to play against righties and lefties alike. He has a very intriguing curveball, while also throwing a changeup and a sweeper, and scouts have raved about his makeup. The Giants were able to draft Bolemon because they acquired the competitive balance-round pick from the Cleveland Guardians in the Patrick Bailey trade, and ultimately those two will forever be linked. That trade will remain something of a “TBD” until we learn how good Bolemon can be, and we’re still many years away from that. Until then, we can look forward to seeing the youngster on the mound in 2027 for his professional debut, as he didn’t pitch (other than in unofficial games) post-draft. It will be interesting to see whether the Giants have Bolemon begin the year in the Arizona Complex League, or if they get him out at the start of the season by sending him to Low-A San Jose. Now let’s add to the list! As a reminder, voting takes place in the comment section. item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene
item.description: …Urges enforcement of life jacket, passenger capacity regulations By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State following the boat mishap that claimed 32 lives. Udoette, who was accompanied by the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Saka Ajao Adewale, visited the area on Monday to interact with marine transport workers and the Red Cross rescue team and receive updates on the ongoing search and recovery operation. During the visit, reports from the rescue site indicated that additional bodies had been recovered, raising the death toll from 29 to 32. The AIG commiserated with the Bayelsa State Government and residents over the tragedy, while commending President Bola Tinubu for his response and expression of sympathy following the incident. She expressed concern over alleged violations of maritime safety regulations, particularly the overloading of the vessel and failure to comply with life jacket requirements. According to her, the boat reportedly conveyed more than 500 passengers despite having a carrying capacity of 200. Udoette urged the state Ministry of Transport and marine unions to strengthen enforcement of safety regulations, particularly compulsory life jacket use and compliance with approved passenger limits. She also called for strict enforcement against operators who flout safety rules, stressing that passengers must take personal responsibility for their safety. Speaking with journalists, the AIG said she visited the waterside on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police to sympathise with the victims’ families and assess the situation. “I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa CP on behalf of the Inspector General of Police to sympathise with the people that died in the incident. I register our condolences and wish the injured quick recovery. “Besides, the maritime personnel told us of the refusal of passengers to obey safety rules, and the boat captain loaded over 500 persons for a boat with a 200-person capacity. That was a suicide mission and a disaster waiting to happen,” she said. Describing the deaths as avoidable, Udoette urged passengers and marine transport operators to comply with established safety regulations. “Some of these deaths are avoidable deaths. Many of the passengers refuse to obey safety rules. My Bible tells me obedience is better than sacrifice. There are rules and regulations on life jackets and overloading, but they refused. “For the living, this is a big lesson to everyone that wants to use a boat for their journey. They should listen to the rules. People should use common sense. This disaster is avoidable,” she added. The post Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: BYU has never won a Maui Invitational championship. How can this year’s Cougars change that?
item.description: BYU players prepare to take the court against Ohio State on Nov. 2, 2026, at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City. | BYU Photo LAHAINA, Hawaii — The Lahaina Civic Center gymnasium is packed with history. Banners hang from its rafters commemorating past Maui Invitational champions, with Duke, North Carolina and Kansas dominating the count. Walls of the arena are dedicated to former Maui standouts and tournament MVPs, such as Kemba Walker, Adam Morrison, Bobby Hurley and Penny Hardaway. Nowhere to be found in the historic gym, however, is a lasting trace of BYU, despite the Cougars having participated in the Maui Invitational there four times before. In fact, as BYU makes its fifth-ever Maui appearance this week, the Cougars are now tied with San Diego State for the second-most times playing in the event without capturing a championship there. Only Memphis has made more trips to Maui (six) without ever hoisting the Wayne Duke trophy, which is presented to the lone unbeaten team after three days of hoops. Additionally, BYU has never produced an invitational MVP, and only one former Cougar — Tyler Haws in 2014 — has landed on the All-Tournament team. Given the current state of both November multi-team events and college basketball as a whole, perhaps 2026 will be the last time BYU graces the Civic Center hardwood in Lahaina and drains shots on the arena’s famous “soft rims.” It’s a shame that one of the sport’s most unique and prestigious early-season traditions is viewed as “on life support” and facing “an uncertain future.” The Protect College Sports Act could easily receive increased support from every political side if it included provisions to save the Maui Invitational — but that’s a thought for another day. If this week truly is the Cougars’ last dance in Maui, it’s their last chance to be crowned champions of the event. And it may be the best such chance they’ve ever had to do so. BYU (No. 25 in KenPom) opens its Maui slate Monday against Washington (No. 88), then will face either Ole Miss (No. 27) or Clemson (No. 75) on Tuesday. Two wins would put the Cougars in Wednesday’s title game, where many fans and pundits anticipate them to meet fellow Big 12 foe Arizona, assuming the Wildcats can survive their bracket of Colorado State, Providence and VCU. Not since 1992 has BYU reached the Maui championship game. The Cougars will likely be favored on both Monday and Tuesday, and in a situation with three games in three days, anything can happen in that third game — even toppling Arizona, if need be. “A lot of it’s going to come down to just toughness,” BYU head coach Kevin Young said of the invitational’s rapid-fire format. “I think our guys possess a lot of that.” BYU’s first time in Maui, 1992, saw the Cougars finish as runners-up, beating No. 9 Oklahoma and then Penny Hardaway-led Memphis before falling to Grant Hill, Bobby Hurley and No. 1 Duke in the championship. item.title: Mountain West Football Rankings: Week 12. Lots of fighting at the bottom.
item.description: Nov 20, 2026; Colorado Springs, Colorado, USA; Air Force Falcons quarterback Evan Medders (5) runs with the ball in the second quarter against the UTEP Miners at Falcon Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The college football season is firing on all cylinders, and games are happening every weekend. The rankings are back for another week. Read on to see how this week’s slate of games affected each team’s status in the MWCConnection Mountain West rankings. 1) New Mexico (0) The Lobos bounced back, playing a tough Wyoming team and coming away with a victory. For one game at least, the offense looked more efficient. It will be interesting to see whether they stick with the quarterback change or go more matchup-based over the next two weeks. Regardless, New Mexico is still the best team in the conference, even if the gap between them and the rest of the conference has been closed a bit. 2) Air Force (+1) The Falcons remain hot despite losing a plethora of players due to injury, and that number continues to mount each week. Despite it all, they sit at nine wins and have a good chance to reach double-digits by the end of the year. UTEP had no answer for the triple option attack, as Air Force piled up nearly 600 yards of total offense. They are a team no one wants to face, which is vintage AFA. 3) Wyoming (-1) The Cowboys lost a tough one, keeping the score close despite not playing their best game. The season has still been a massive success for the program, and playing a competitive game without their sensational starting quarterback still counts for something. While Wyoming doesn’t control their own destiny, they are still in play to make the conference championship game, which was unthinkable in September. 4) UNLV (0) The Rebels also didn’t play their best game this weekend, but were able to come away with the victory anyway, which is a sign of progress for them. The conference’s most inconsistent teams this year notched their seventh win, once again on the shoulders of their starting quarterback. UNLV lives and dies with the highlights and turnovers of Jackson Arnold, but it’s always worth watching. 5) North Dakota State (0) The Bison jumped out to a huge lead, and then held on for a victory against the worst team in FBS football. The grind of the season seems to have gotten to them, as they haven’t looked quite the same in the second half of the season. Still, North Dakota State is winning games and will be going to a bowl game in their first FBS season, and that is quite an accomplishment. 6) Nevada (+1) The Wolf Pack gutted out a win against someone in their own competency tier. They won mainly on the strength of their field goal unit, which accounted for 9 of their 16 points on the evening. The offense shouldn’t be mistaken for a good unit but they moved the ball on the ground, which helped them throughout the evening. item.title: Nontendered players to pique the Phillies’ interest
item.description: ANAHEIM, CALIFORNIA - JULY 19: Matt Vierling #8 of the Detroit Tigers at bat during the game against the Los Angeles Angels at Angel Stadium of Anaheim on July 19, 2026 in Anaheim, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The deadline to tender contracts to arbitration eligible players has come and gone, meaning the free agent market has once again been flooded with prospective players. Usually, there are some surprises included in that batch, but for the most part, stock held true. The Phillies were included in this group, sending out offers to players that should help them in 2027 while pruning the extra roster spots for future use. This new crop of players from which the Phillies can sift through does have some interesting names that match some of the needs the team has. Them not getting a contract offer means that some of the warts they possess were too much to spend money on, but there can still be a bargain or two if looking hard enough. It’s not the greatest of players to choose from, but hey – you never know! Let’s look at some of those players the Phillies could have an interest in this offseason. Davis Schneider – If finding a player that can play multiple positions defensively while also batting from the right side is a goal of the offseason, signing Schneider is an option. There’s just one little bitty problem: Schneider kind of stinks. He’s played left field and second base in 2026, third base a few times in 2025….and hit like a backup catcher. He doesn’t chase that much, which is a nice skill to have, but so is actually making contact with the ball. He showed flashes of what he could do in 2025 when he posted a 118 OPS+ by hitting for some pop and showing a good amount of patience, but he fell back to Earth in 2026, hitting a paltry .145/.310/.315 (77 OPS+). Bringing him onto the roster would at least bolster the bench a bit, but this one feels like a player that could be had on a minor league deal. Probably don’t want to guarantee much of anything. Gabriel Arias – How would you like to have a backup shortstop that has not had a season in which he hit above an 83 OPS+ or had an on base percentage that crested .300? Yes? Well have I got a guy for you to look at. Arias does hit the ball hard when he hits it, but he also swings the bat at the plate like there is a bee about to sting him. Yet you wouldn’t be interested in him for his bat as much as for his glove. He’s still able to play a high level defense at multiple positions and has at least some ability to pop a baseball out. Sound familiar < coughcheapEdmundoSosacough >? Andrew Saalfrank – With a dearth of left handed pitching in their own system, adding Saalfrank will give them at least someone who has had recent major league success and give them something of a different look. item.title: Winners, Losers, and Honorable Mentions from an embarrassing UNC loss to Virginia
item.description: CHARLOTTESVILLE, VIRGINIA - NOVEMBER 21: Travis Burgess #3 of the North Carolina Tar Heels throws apart pass in front of Fisher Camac #14 of the Virginia Cavaliers in the first half during a game at Scott Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Charlottesville, Virginia. (Photo by Ryan M. Kelly/Getty Images) | Getty Images In season where UNC fans felt like they had been in every game, Saturday’s result in Charlottesville was nothing short of, like the title says, embarrassing. The Tar Heels played like they hadn’t taken preparation for the Cavaliers seriously, and after the promise of a 5-4 record following the UConn win, the Tar Heels are dangerously close to needing a special dispensation to play in a bowl game with a three game losing streak to end the season. There was a little good worth pointing out but a lot of bad. Let’s dive in, shall we? Winners Travis Burgess- We could play the game of putting him as both a winner and loser, but look, the freshman getting his first start showed out and really wasn’t the reason why Carolina lost. 25-45, 354 yards with a long pass of 46 yards, and was also the leading rusher with 106 net yards. It’s enough to make fans wonder “what exactly were they waiting for to play him?” If this staff is truly about the development, then letting the young Burgess get some of his mistakes over with early would have led to a more seasoned player by this point that could have really lit up in the Petrino offense. Based on the recruiting it’s pretty clear that Burgess is seen as next year’s starter at least. Yes the two interceptions were killer, but it would have been nice if he had been able to get them out earlier in the season. Jordan Shipp- You think he was happy to have a quarterback that has a livelier arm? No touchdown catches but nine catches for an astounding 149 yards. On a day where Carolina lost Jelani Thurman early they needed their other pass catching star to step up and he did. At this point what else can you say about him except if he is back in a UNC uniform next year along with Burgess, that could be a very fun combo. Mason Humphrey- The transfer from Lehigh hadn’t exactly put up the stats this season as Shipp, Thurman, and the running backs had mostly been the ones to take the bulk of the work from Billy Edwards, Jr. Somehow, though, he just magically appeared to haul in three catches for 95 yards and show why he was brought in from the FCS school. Here’s hoping against the Wolfpack next week he can have a repeat performance. Losers UNC Secondary- Beau Pribula just had it too easy on Saturday. He completed 79% of his passes, didn’t get picked off, and had four touchdown passes. They were also eaten alive by Jekail Middlebrook. Middlebrook chewed up the backfield for 140 yards including the absolute backbreaker 75-yard touchdown catch after the Tar Heels finally put together a decent drive. item.title: Josh Jacobs not expected to play vs Rams
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams could be catching a break against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Green Bay is not expecting running back Josh Jacobs to play as he continues recovering from surgery to repair a fractured right ring finger. His expected absence could further complicate an already struggling Packers rushing attack and give the Rams’ defense another reason to anticipate a pass-heavy offensive approach. Josh Jacobs, with his surgically repaired right ring finger heavily protected, is giving it a go even though coach Matt LaFleur said he didn’t think it was very likely that Jacobs could play on Wednesday. Jacobs would need to convince them he could hold onto the football for… pic.twitter.com/LYcXBBV50p — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) November 21, 2026 Jacobs suffered the injury during Green Bay’s Week 9 victory over the New England Patriots and underwent surgery on November 13. Although he has returned to individual work, head coach Matt LaFleur indicated that Jacobs remains unlikely to suit up against Los Angeles. He will need to demonstrate that he can properly handle the football before returning to game action. It has been an incredibly up-and-down season for Jacobs. He missed the first six games while on the Commissioner’s Exempt List following off-field legal issues before returning in Week 7. Unfortunately, his return has not gone as planned. Across three appearances, Jacobs has recorded just 80 rushing yards on 36 carries, averaging a career-low 2.2 yards per attempt. Green Bay has struggled to establish consistency on the ground throughout the season. Through its first eight games, the Packers averaged just 60.6 rushing yards per game, one of the worst marks in the NFL. Even with Jacobs sidelined, the backfield has struggled to provide a dependable alternative. Without Jacobs, the Rams can enter Wednesday’s matchup with a clearer expectation of what Green Bay wants to do offensively. While Kaleb Johnson and the other available running backs will still get opportunities, Los Angeles can focus more attention on slowing down the passing game. That doesn’t mean the Packers will abandon the run entirely, but the Rams should have fewer reasons to fear a consistent ground attack. With the opportunity to make Green Bay one-dimensional, Los Angeles’ pass rush and secondary could play a significant role in determining the outcome.

item.title: Yankees Potential Free Agent Target: Kaima Taira
item.description: YOKOHAMA, JAPAN - JULY 31: Relief pitcher Kaima Taira #61 of Team Japan pitches in the eighth inning against Team Mexico during the baseball opening round Group A game on day eight of the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games at Yokohama Baseball Stadium on July 31, 2021 in Yokohama, Kanagawa, Japan. (Photo by Yuichi Masuda/Getty Images) | 2021 Getty Images In a free agent class that falls off a cliff beyond the recently-signed Tarik Skubal, there’s an intriguing cadre of Japanese players entering the market. Teruaki Sato, Hiromi Itoh, and Kaima Taira have all been posted by their NPB clubs. The trio has torn up their home soil and appear ready to test their skills stateside, though the pending lockout means that the players must sign by 11:59pm ET on December 1st. Sato is the name to which the Yankees have been most concretely linked given the need at third base, but Taira also deserves their interest given his unique skillset on the mound. 2026 Statistics (NPB): 23 games (22 starts), 146 IP, 12-5, 1.36 ERA, 2.28 FIP, 2.83 xFIP, 24.8% K%, 7.9% BB%, 0.96 WHIP 2027 FanGraphs Depths Charts Projections: 24 games started, 139 IP, 8-9, 4.46 ERA, 4.39 FIP, 18.9% K%, 9.3% BB%, 1.44 WHIP, 1.4 fWAR Taira has been a Swiss Army knife pitcher during his eight-year career for the Seibu Lions. He has experience in the rotation, starting 23 games in 2023 and 22 games this past season. He was the team’s principal closer for two seasons, racking up 20 saves in 2021 and 34 in 2025. The other four seasons he operated as a swingman, capable of making a spot start but mostly getting deployed an inning at a time in relief. The 2020 Pacific League Rookie of the Year set an NPB record with 39 consecutive scoreless appearances in 2021 and even pitched a combined no-hitter, finishing a game started by current Astro Tatsuya Imai on April 18, 2025. He is a four-time All-Star in NPB but had to withdraw from Japan’s 2026 WBC roster after suffering a calf strain shortly before the tournament. There is always a question of how Japanese pitchers will adjust to the jump from facing NPB hitters to those in MLB. Shohei Ohtani aside, over the last decade Yoshinobu Yamamoto stands apart as the lone outlier who seemingly got better after making the switch. Other high-profile names including Imai, Yusei Kikuchi, and Roki Sasaki experienced significant growing pains upon their introduction to the league and have never quite hit the heights of their NPB days now that they are facing much tougher competition (though Kikuchi has at least made a couple All-Star teams). Taira’s NPB career falls somewhere between Yamamoto and the duo of Imai and Kikuchi — never quite as dominant in Japan as Yamamoto but significantly better at run prevention than Imai or Kikuchi. In eight seasons, he has pitched to a 1.78 ERA in 592 innings between the rotation and bullpen, allowing right around one baserunner per inning and striking out almost three times as many batters as he walks. item.title: Adrian Morejon rejects QO, who emerges as Padres LH relief options
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers LH reliever Alex Vesia could be a potential free-agent signing. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images As expected, Adrian Morejon rejected the San Diego Padres’ one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer. While the Friar Faithful were disappointed by his decision, the door has not closed on Morejon returning to San Diego. However, the Padres cannot afford to wait and risk losing an opportunity to sign a top free-agent left-handed reliever. The free-agent market offers multiple candidates who have a proven track record of recording outs in late-inning pressure situations. Implications from Morejon’s decision The thought of Morejon not wearing the Brown & Gold is disappointing but feels inevitable. He is one of the premier free agent pitchers available, and multiple suitors will aggressively vie for him. After all, what franchise isn’t in the market for a hard-throwing left-handed reliever? Suddenly, bullpen reconstruction will become a priority if Morejon leaves town. Friars President of Baseball Operations & General Manager A.J. Preller will be forced to add another bullpen arm alongside the game’s top closer, Mason Miller. Guaranteed, he has already identified several lefty targets if his worst nightmare becomes reality. Other teams are chasing the same needs; the Padres must bid aggressively on their top targets or risk getting left behind. Filling the void: Morejon’s replacement options Replacing Morejon is a slightly different task than searching for a lefty specialist. The Padres need to sign a left-handed reliever who can handle a similar workload. Morejon has appeared in 151 games over the last two seasons. The Friars already have plenty of left-handed bullpen depth, led by Kyle Hart, Yuki Matsui, and Wandy Peralta. However, each is brought in to face one or two left-handed hitters and end a potential scoring threat. The Padres will enter the market and look to add a proven left-handed setup reliever who can pitch multiple innings. Their eyes should be on Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Alex Vesia, who has success as a setup reliever. He is the ideal replacement for Morejon; his mound presence ensures the bullpen retains last season’s dominant edge. View Link Vesia posted a 2.64 ERA, a 1.069 WHIP, and struck out 73 batters in 58.0 innings pitched. He cannot match Morejon’s velocity, but Vesia averaged 11.5 strikeouts per nine innings, well above last season’s major league average. He misses bats and induces opposing batters to hit into double plays with his vertical dropping four-seam fastball. Chicago White Sox Sean Newcomb is the next best free-agent option. He may not be in the class of Morejon or Vesia, but Newcomb posted a 3.09 ERA over 90.1 innings pitched in 60 appearances. Opponents struggle to make consistent contact (.233 BA) off him. Newcomb’s 95 MPH fastball induces plenty of swings and misses by challenging hitters in the strike zone. His success thrives on locating his fastball and avoiding walk

item.title: Fernando Mendoza shows his mettle as Broncos gallop past Raiders 38-24
item.description: (Photo by Justin Tafoya/Getty Images) | Getty Images What looked like a runaway division win by the Denver Broncos instead turned into Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback showcasing his mettle on a brisk Mile High Sunday afternoon. Facing yet another stingy defense, the Silver & Black’s prized No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft had his moments of inaccuracy and panic — as expected from a rookie quarterback — but the Indiana product showed off his arm talent, mental toughness, and poise that made Mendoza worthy of the top overall selection, despite a tough 38-24 division defeat. At the forefront of the Raiders offense, Mendoza helped orchestrate a trio of touchdown drives, much to the chagrin of Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph. Las Vegas franchise quarterback’s first official touchdown was a beauty of a loft to running back Ashton Jeanty who torched Denver outside linebacker Que Robinson on a wheel route for a 68-yard catch-and-run, to trim the disadvantage to 17-10 before halftime. And in the third quarter, Mendoza displayed a filthy handoff fake that froze elite cornerback Pat Surtain II and allowed veteran tight end Ian Thomas to slither past for a 19-yard touchdown to tie the ball game at 17 apiece. Make that TWO TDs for Fernando Mendoza 🗣️ LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sgnbFG3sUr — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 Even after Denver sprinted ahead with back-to-back touchdown drives after Las Vegas tied the contest to take a 31-17 lead, Mendoza didn’t wilt — even with the Raiders in obvious passing mode trying to catch up. The 6-foot-5 and 225-pound quarterback went 7-for-7 during an eight-play, 69-yard scoring drive that showed the variety of throws Mendoza can make. From short strikes to a long ball (39-yard dime to fleet-footed wide receiver Tre Tucker), the 23-year-old spread the ball around before finding wideout Jack Bech for a seven-yard touchdown pass. Initially called just short of the end zone, replay assist noted Bech held the ball over the goal line for the score, 31-24, Broncos. And that’s as close as Las Vegas (4-7 overall) would get in the first of two AFC West matchups with Denver this season. Looking to knot the game once more, Mendoza telegraphed his throw on a slant route to Tucker after the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter and Broncos slot cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian read the play to perfection and snagged the pass for a one-hand interception and housed the takeaway for the pick six, 38-24 Denver. The #Broncos have had recent talks with CB Ja’Quan McMillan on a contract extension to no avail. The price just went up. pic.twitter.com/tQ3YuUkBLA — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 23, 2026 Denver head coach Sean Payton — who has his hard-charging Broncos ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs for the AFC West title despite both being 8-2 overall and 3-1 in division play — noted he can see a potential Raiders resurgence with Mendoza under center. “A much different Raiders team

item.title: Syracuse men’s basketball: fans don’t have to pretend all wins are good ones
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Syracuse, New York, USA; Syracuse Orange head coach Gerry McNamara reacts during the second half against the Lafayette Leopards at the JMA Wireless Dome. Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After watching the Syracuse Orange struggle with Cornell on Wednesday, I assumed that Saturday’s game would bring out a focused, energetic squad. That didn’t happen and after having to pull out all the stops to win 84-81 over a Lafayette team that had lost by 36 to Butler and 28 to St. Bonaventure, Gerry McNamara was asked a question about the margin of victory in the wins this week. “I don’t worry. I’ll let other people worry about that nonsense, bullshit, I don’t care. Win a game you know. That’s how I grew up…..I’m not going to worry about margin of victory, all that. I know the next game I play I’m going to coach to win again. So I don’t worry about al the other stuff because at the end of the day you’re still going to have those opponents to play anyway so if you beat them, the margin of victory doesn’t, just win the game you’re playing in front of you. So my focus is on can we continue to get better.” McNamara ended the answer by talking about shooting and offense, but is that the issue? Can we talk about Syracuse’s defense giving up 80+ points to two teams this week? What about the fact that Cornell and Lafayette went 24-54 from 3 in the two games? Unfortunately for anyone who wants to espouse “Just win baby”, it’s not the case in today’s college basketball. Syracuse built their schedule around the NET formula and margin of victory against teams ranked 200th and 303rd in this morning’s KenPom is a factor. Winning 20 or 21 games might not be enough for an invite when the ACC is not off to a strong start. Right now Syracuse sits 81st in KenPom. Last year’s sub-500 team finished the year ranked 87th and the lowest ranked NCAA at-large team was Missouri who was 54th. Yes, it’s early. Yes, you have to win the games, but you cannot pretend that this shouldn’t be a concern….because it is. He went on to talk about not having juice, but why wait until it’s 20+ minutes in the game to make an adjustment to the press? This is still a young staff and they sure don’t seem to have a grasp on what they want this team to be this season. If you’re heading into desperation mode against Lafayette, even with two starters injured, that’s a big warning sign. This was a November game that almost turned into a unfathomable loss and it wasn’t the time to lecture anyone about playing to win the game. I’m sensititve to the fact that Gerry’s dealing with a lot right now- on and off the court. I’m worried that the pressure he’s putting on himself to get this program back is too much, but you can’t get this agitated over a legitimate question. He didn’t mention ISIS , but there were a lot of Shafer vibes coming out of this one….let’s hope the Albany post-game talk stays out of “cutting people’s heads off” talk.

item.title: GametimeCT Top 10 Football Poll, Week 12 (Nov. 23): Teams prepare for Thanksgiving Week, playoffs
item.description: Justin Daniel, left, of St. Joseph runs the ball against Greenwich on November 14, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) Only 22 CIAC football games were played across the state last week, with only three Top 10 teams competing. With most of the state gearing up for Thanksgiving Week, the Top 10 remained unchanged as we enter the regular season finale. All three of the Top 10 teams that did play this past week earned victories, including No. 1 St. Joseph, No. 7 New Britain and No. 8 Pomperaug. No. 3 Hand and No. 4 New Canaan are the only other two teams to earn over 500 points in the voting, while No. 5 Masuk and No. 6 Greenwich are in the 400-point range. No. 8 New Britain, No. 9 Pomperaug (both of which wrapped up their regular season's this past week) and No. 9 Southington all have over 300 points while No. 10 Staples sits at 282. On the cusp of the Top 10 are undefeated New London with 252 points and Cheshire, which has losses to Hand and Staples this season, with 215 points. item.title: 2026-27 Mountain West Basketball Power Rankings: Nov. 23
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 19: Tyrin Jones #6 of the UNLV Rebels drives to the basket against Christian Gurdak #32 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the second half during the Seventh Place game in the Players Era 8 bracket of The 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at Michelob ULTRA Arena on November 19, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Players Era/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the most exciting times of the college basketball season has arrived: Feast week! A few Mountain West programs have already began their feast week festivities, while others won’t until December. Which teams moved up — and down — in this week’s rankings? Let’s dive into it! 1. Grand Canyon Skinny: Grand Canyon did not play a game this week, but they have a big test Tuesday against Saint Louis and Wednesday against either Stanford or Colorado. 2. Wyoming Skinny: We have a new No. 2 this week, as Wyoming moved to 5-1 with wins over Sam Houston State and Duquesne. Naz Meyer continues to look outstanding, although I do want to shout out Uriyah Rojas. The former Community College All-American blossomed this week, averaging 18.0 points on 44.0 percent shooting (8-15 3P) in 23.5 minutes in those two games. He couldn’t quite find his footing in a limited role this year, but appears to have established himself as. more reliable rotation player thus far. 3. Nevada Skinny: Nevada head coach Steve Alford sent a message this week by benching Elijah Price and Vaughn Weems amid a slow start to the season. Well, the message was received, as they combined for 32 points off the bench in the Wolf Pack’s 17-point win against Idaho this week. Price tallied a game-high 21 points with seven rebounds, one steal and one block, while Weems had 11 points and a team-high six dimes. 4. New Mexico Skinny: To be clear: I don’t think New Mexico will be in this spot for long. But you can’t justify staying in the top-3 after getting smacked by Wichita State by 25 — the Lobos got absolutely demolished in the second half. The Shockers shot 56.7 percent from the floor to the Lobos’ 26.7 percent. Beyond Jake Hall’s 16 points, Uriah Tenette, Hudson Mayes and Fynn Lasting all shot a combined 7-of-29. 5. UNLV Skinny: For the second-straight year, the Players’ Era proved to be way too big of a test for UNLV, who cracked the top-3 in last week’s rankings! Well, they came crashing down to earth with three losses to Kansas, Auburn and Rutgers, respectively. Those aren’t easy games, but the Runnin’ Rebels did lost by an average of 19.7 points. Ranking them right in the middle feels appropriate. 6. UTEP Skinny: UTEP put together a much better showing this week against New Mexico State after last week’s rock fight. They also smacked Florida A&M, one of the nation’s worst Division-I programs, by 33 at home. They are still forcing turnovers on nearly a quarter of opponents’ possessions (24.7 percent), a top-15 mark in the country, and they’re doing a good job corralling extra opportunities.

item.title: The Big Ten is the best conference in women’s college basketball—and not for the reasons you think
item.description: Shauna Green and Berry Wallace. (Photo by Michael Hickey) | Getty Images The Big Ten is the deepest conference in women’s college basketball. The conference is currently projected by ESPN to have 13 teams make the NCAA Tournament: Michigan — No. 1 seed USC — No. 1 seed Iowa — No. 3 seed UCLA — No. 3 seed Washington — No. 4 seed Maryland — No. 4 seed Ohio State — No. 5 seed Illinois — No. 5 seed Minnesota — No. 6 seed Nebraska — No. 6 seed Michigan State — No. 7 seed Oregon — No. 9 seed Indiana — No. 10 seed The teams currently occupying seeds No. 1 through No. 4 are getting plenty of attention, while No. 5-seed Ohio State has been to 30 Big Dances, including the last five in a row, so they’re not exactly under the radar. However, the six other teams on the list all are, to some extent, flying under the radar—until those top-seven teams begin to find out that none of the middle-of-the-pack teams will be easy to beat, leaving the Big Ten wide open. Let’s take a look at where the Big Ten’s six mid-rangers are in the early stages of this season. In the comments, let us know which of the six squads you could see emerging as the biggest threat to the conference’s expected titans. Illinois (No. 21 in AP poll) NCAA Tournament track record: Has never been to Elite Eight; last Sweet 16: 1998; last Round of 32: 2026; total NCAA Tournaments: 11 (3 in last 4 years; last before that was 2003) Berry Wallace is the player to watch for the Fighting Illini. She was their representative on the All-Big Ten First Team last year; she also made preseason First Team after averaging 18.4 points per game and 6.2 rebounds per game in 2025-26. She shot 86.5 percent from the charity stripe on 4.1 attempts per contest. As a freshman in 2024-25, she shot 39.8 percent from deep with 35 makes. So far this year, she’s 27-for-41 (65.9 percent) from the field (16th in the nation) and 7-for-10 from 3 with 19 points per game. Last season, Illinois beat then-No. 7 Maryland on Jan. 1 and peaked at No. 25 on Jan. 12. They went on to also beat then-No. 25 Washington and then-No. 18 Michigan State, with the latter victory coming in the Big Ten Tournament. They earned a No. 7 seed in the NCAA Tournament and advanced to the second round. Head coach Shauna Green took over in 2022-23 and improved on the program’s 2021-22 season by 12.5 games, finishing 22-10, including 11-7 in the Big Ten after the team had gone 1-13. Green has led a program, which prior to her taking over hadn’t made the Big Dance since 2003, to three tourneys in four years, including the Round of 32 the past two years. Minnesota (No. 17 in AP poll) NCAA Tournament track record: Has never been to championship game; last Final Four: 2004 (also last Elite Eight); last Sweet 16: 2026; total NCAA Tournaments: 11 (last year was 1st since 2018) The Golden Gophers got their taste of Sweet 16 glory last year, but they’ve lost NCAA Tournament hero Amaya Battle to graduation. They also lost leading scorer Tori McKinney to a season-end

item.title: England's Freeman in contention for All Blacks rematch
item.description: Freeman has 11 tries in 31 matches for England [Getty Images] England wing Tommy Freeman is in contention for Saturday's Nations Championship play-off meeting with New Zealand. The 25-year-old has been a key part of England's backline this year, starting nine Tests in a row for before being rotated out of the side for their comprehensive win over Japan on 14 November. He was due to return for the 37-12 win over the All Blacks on Saturday, but a thigh issue forced his withdrawal in the hours before kick-off. Harlequins' Cadan Murley was called into the side to replace Freeman and impressed in an emphatic England performance. Head coach Steve Borthwick has bolstered his back-three options, which also include Gloucester's Will Joseph, by calling up Saracens' 20-year-old Noah Caluori. Caluori, who finished as joint-top try scorer in last year's Prem alongside Freeman, crossed on his England debut against Fiji in July and was a late replacement in the win over Argentina a week later. He also scored two tries in a England A's win over an Argentine equivalent earlier this month. Fly-half Fin Smith, who came off 55 minutes into the win over the All Blacks with cramp, is also in a 37-strong squad who have gathered at England's training base to prepare for Saturday's third-place play-off. England finished a point short of France in the northern hemisphere standings of the new format, missing out on a place in Sunday's Nations Championship final against South Africa. The result of England and New Zealand's meeting, along with the weekend's other five matches at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium, will contribute to a Ryder Cup-style points race for the inaugural hemisphere shield. England squad to face New Zealand Forwards: Fin Baxter (Harlequins), Ollie Chessum (Leicester Tigers), Arthur Clark (Gloucester Rugby), Alex Coles (Northampton Saints), Luke Cowan-Dickie (Sale Sharks), Ben Curry (Sale Sharks), Theo Dan (Saracens), Ben Earl (Saracens), Greg Fisilau (Exeter Chiefs), Jamie George (Saracens), Ellis Genge (Bristol Bears), Joe Heyes (Leicester Tigers), Maro Itoje (Saracens), Emmanuel Iyogun (Northampton Saints), Jack Kenningham (Harlequins), George Martin (Saracens), Asher Opoku-Fordjour (Sale Sharks), Tom Pearson (Northampton Saints), Henry Pollock (Northampton Saints), Will Stuart (Bath Rugby) Backs: Seb Atkinson (Gloucester Rugby), Noah Calouri (Saracens), Fraser Dingwall (Northampton Saints), George Ford (Sale Sharks), Tommy Freeman (Northampton Saints), George Furbank (Harlequins), Will Joseph (Gloucester Rugby), Joe Marchant (Sale Sharks), Cadan Murley (Harlequins), Archie McParland (Northampton Saints), Max Ojomoh (Bath Rugby), Henry Slade (Exeter Chiefs), Fin Smith (Northampton Saints), Marcus Smith (Harlequins), Ben Spencer (Bath Rugby), Freddie Steward (Leicester Tigers), Jack van Poortvliet (Leicester Tigers) Listen: Sport's Strangest Crimes - Bloodgate Listen to the latest Rugby Union Weekly podcast

item.title: Nigeria records 94% HIV viral suppression – NACA
item.description: The NACA director-general, however, identified gaps in HIV diagnosis, stressing the need to ensure more Nigerians know their status and access uninterrupted treatment. She said Early Infant Diagnosis coverage among HIV-exposed infants increased from 15 per cent in 2022 to 66 per cent in 2025. “While this is significant progress, we must do more to ensure that no child is left behind,” Ilori said. She said the 2026 World AIDS Day theme, “Ending AIDS Starts with Access: Equity, Ownership and Sustainability,” highlighted the need for equitable access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care. “Access must not depend on where you live, what you earn or who you are. It is a right, not a privilege,” she said. Ilori announced that NACA would unveil the National HIV Domestic Resource Mobilisation and Sustainability Strategy 2026–2030 on Dec. 1, as part of the World AIDS Day commemoration. According to her, the strategy will strengthen domestic financing, promote national ownership and sustain Nigeria’s HIV response amid declining global health funding. She also announced plans for a National Prevention Conference to explore innovative HIV prevention approaches, including self-testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and emerging prevention technologies. Dr Adebobola Bashorun, National Coordinator, National AIDS, Viral Hepatitis and STIs Control Programme (NASCP), said innovations would only save lives if they were accessible and affordable. “We can have the best technology and products, but without access they are useless,” he said. Bashorun said Nigeria was scaling up injectable HIV prevention medicines, oral PrEP and interventions to prevent mother-to-child transmission. UNAIDS Country Director, Ms Tina Boonto, said more than 1.5 million Nigerians living with HIV were accessing antiretroviral treatment. She, however, said Nigeria recorded about 64,000 new HIV infections annually, far above the fewer than 5,000 required to end AIDS as a public health threat. “Ending AIDS starts with ensuring everyone can access the services, medicines, technologies and information they need,” she said. Boonto called for increased HIV testing, expanded prevention services and stronger efforts to eliminate mother-to-child transmission. Dr Patrick Dakum, Executive Officer, Institute for Human Virology (IHVN), represented by the Director of Prevention, Care and Treatment, Dr Helen Omuh, stressed the need for equitable access to HIV services, community ownership and sustained domestic commitment. Dakum, speaking on behalf of implementing partners, reaffirmed their commitment to expanding effective interventions, strengthening domestic ownership and financing, and promoting sustainability. “We want to affirm that ending AIDS requires more than service availability. It requires equitable access, empowered communities, strong national ownership and sustainable investment. “So together, we can build a resilient HIV response and accelerate Nigeria’s progress towards ending A

item.title: Four die as Omo-Agege survives alleged assassination attempt in Delta
item.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Deputy Senate President and Delta Central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has survived an alleged assassination attempt during a campaign tour of Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The attack, which occurred during a campaign visit, reportedly left four persons dead and four others critically injured. The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation, in a statement by its Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, said armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage at close range while he was addressing a crowd that had gathered to receive him. According to the organisation, Omo-Agege escaped being hit by bullets, which allegedly passed close to his head. It identified two of the deceased as its aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro. The statement also named the injured as Chief Evance Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho, adding that they were receiving medical attention. The organisation said eyewitnesses alleged that the attackers were heard shouting, “It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill,” describing the incident as a targeted assassination attempt rather than a political clash. However, a video obtained by Vanguard showed some NDC supporters lying bloodied on the floor of a hospital. When Vanguard contacted some eyewitnesses, one of them, Pius Eguono, said, “We were all shot in the crowd, but Efemena Umukoro has been killed. I’m on the run.” The post Four die as Omo-Agege survives alleged assassination attempt in Delta appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu, Sanwo-Olu court Igbo community ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: …Urge national cohesion, economic inclusion By Olasunkanmi Akoni President Bola Tinubu and Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, have urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and regional divisions, emphasising the need for national cohesion, mutual understanding and inclusive economic development. The leaders made the call on Monday at the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. The engagement, attended by Igbo community leaders, business stakeholders and government officials, provided an opportunity to strengthen relations between the Igbo community and the Lagos and Federal Governments ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing participants, Tinubu urged Nigerians to embrace a shared national identity, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or regional backgrounds, saying the country’s development depended on the collective contributions of all citizens. He also stressed the importance of creating broad-based economic opportunities to enable Nigerians to contribute meaningfully to nation-building. “We must see ourselves as one people with a shared future. “Nigeria must rise above its divisions, because our true development depends on the active participation and commitment of every single citizen, regardless of background,” the President said. Earlier, Sanwo-Olu commended Tinubu for attending the gathering, describing his presence as an affirmation of the important role played by the Igbo community in the socioeconomic development of Lagos State. He acknowledged the contributions of Igbo political leaders, entrepreneurs, business associates and other stakeholders to the growth of the state. “The President’s presence here today is a significant gesture of recognition for Ndigbo and their rightful place in Lagos. “We deeply value the enduring contributions and longstanding partnerships of the political leaders, business associates, and stakeholders who continue to build this state alongside us,” the governor said. Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey, particularly the political developments of 1999, 2003 and 2007, Sanwo-Olu also paid tribute to past and present leaders whose contributions helped shape the country’s political evolution. The town hall was designed to deepen engagement, address concerns affecting the Igbo community in Lagos and strengthen collaboration between community representatives and the two tiers of government. item.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
item.description: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers. CVE-2026-76466 , which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services. The bug involves hard-coded authentication credentials and insufficient certificate validation in clustered Expressway deployments. “An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands,” Cisco said in October, when it disclosed the bug and issued a software update that fixed the flaw. “A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.” At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability. That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available. “The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices,” F6’s Cyber Defense Center said on Thursday. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.” Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information. The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6. The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices. A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday. Cisco updated its advisory on Monday to acknowledge CISA’s addition, while noting that it has no direct evidence of active exploitation. The Register reached out to the networking and security vendor for additional details about the scope of the attacks, but did not receive any response. We will update this story as we learn more. ®

item.title: NFL Week 11 injury roundup: Saquon Barkley, Bhayshul Tuten and more
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images NFL Week 11 injury roundup: Saquon Barkley, Bhayshul Tuten and more appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sunday slate was not as packed in Week 11 due to Bye-mageddon . Six NFL teams enjoyed some extra rest on Sunday ahead of a packed week of Thanksgiving football matchups. It is reasonable to assume that fewer games would also mean fewer injuries. That is true to a certain extent, but there are still plenty of injuries to go over this week. Aidan Hutchinson’s Week 10 ACL injury became a talking point around the NFL ahead of Week 11. Multiple head coaches around the league urged players to be a bit more careful with their celebrations moving forward. But that didn’t stop players like Cam Skattebo and Jameson Williams from flipping into the end zone when given the opportunity. Either way, injuries can easily turn into a problem for contending teams around this time of year. The playoffs are just over a month away, which means anything more than a minor injury can quickly become a disaster. Plus, long-term injuries can still be dangerous for rebuilding teams as they can linger into the 2027 season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Here are some of the most important injuries that fans need to know about after Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season. Saquon Barkley , Philadelphia Eagles Barkley has been battered and bruised throughout Philly’s disastrous 2026 campaign. He’s already missed multiple games throughout October and November. Unfortunately, Barkley may have picked up yet another injury. Saquon appeared to injure his left arm during the fourth quarter of Sunday’s win over Pittsburgh. He did not return to the game and his status is currently a bit murky. Barkley made some concerning comments after the game, though he still believes he can play on Thanksgiving against the Cowboys. Eagles fans should wait for further updates on his status on Monday. It may also be wise to keep an eye on his practice reports over the next few days. In other Eagles injury news, cornerback Quinyon Mitchell left Sunday’s game with a hamstring injury. Bhayshul Tuten, Jacksonville Jaguars Tuten left Sunday’s loss against the Giants late during the fourth quarter. He limped off the field following an eight-yard run and did not return for the rest of the game. The exact injury injury is currently unclear. This comes in addition to Tuten’s ongoing foot and ankle injuries that have bothered him over the past few weeks. In other Jaguars news, Walker Little (knee) and Jarrian Jones (chest) both suffered injuries on Sunday. Colton McKivitz, San Francisco 49ers The 49ers look like an absolute powerhouse after demolishing the Vikings on Sunday Night Football. But they suffered yet another serious injury, this time on the offensive line. Right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a serious ankle injury and was carted off the field on Sunday night. item.title: Dodgers make ‘intriguing’ signing after losing Tarik Skubal to Mets
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Dodgers make ‘intriguing’ signing after losing Tarik Skubal to Mets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The biggest news from the MLB offseason so far is Tarik Skubal signing a $450 million contract with the New York Mets . Also, reports say the Los Angeles Dodgers didn’t make an offer to Skubal. On Monday, Los Angeles officially announced they signed right-handed relief pitcher Robert Stephenson to a minor-league contract, per Katie Woo of The Athletic. Stephenson missed the 2026 season with the Los Angeles Angels after elbow surgery. According to Woo, the addition to the Dodgers’ pitching staff is “intriguing” as they look to add bullpen depth. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The #Dodgers have signed right-hander Robert Stephenson to a minor-league deal, sources tell me and @Ken_Rosenthal . Was previously with the Angels, but missed all of 2026 after undergoing elbow surgery. An intriguing add as the club focuses on bolstering depth. — Katie Woo (@katiejwoo) November 23, 2026 Additionally, Stephenson joining the Dodgers lets him recover in the minor leagues. The organization will also monitor his progress by not guaranteeing him a roster spot or money up front. The Angels declined Stephenson’s 2027 club option earlier in the year. He made only 12 appearances after signing a three-year, $33 million contract. Stephenson has pitched in MLB since 2016. He’s pitched for the Cincinnati Reds, Colorado Rockies, Pittsburgh Pirates, and Tampa Bay Rays. In 2023, he had a standout season with the Rays, finishing with a 2.35 ERA and 60 strikeouts in 38.1 innings. Skubal finished the 2026 season 12-7 with a 2.73 ERA and 186 strikeouts. He started the season with the Detroit Tigers. In August, the Dodgers acquired Skubal in a trade . Ultimately, Los Angeles won the National League West with a 100-62 record. However, their back-to-back World Series reign ended when the Milwaukee Brewers swept them in the NLCS . The Brewers went on to win the World Series. Skubal won two Cy Young Awards in 2024 and 2025 with the Tigers. Stephenson has a 19-20 record, a 4.59 ERA, and 416 strikeouts. item.title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted. Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for. He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians. Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected. Niger residents gather for an engagement of NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan. The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections. NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes. Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC. Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC. Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027. The post Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: James Gallagher’s MMA career was so much more than the Ricky Bandejas loss
item.description: James Gallagher bidding farewell to mixed martial arts at age 30 on Sunday flooded my mind with memories of him as a teenage prodigy, bustling Bellator Dublin shows and a feeling that despite never realizing the glory he thought he would, his career is one of the most successful in Irish MMA history. A highlight reel of Ricky Bandejas’ 2018 upset of Gallagher will flicker through a lot of people’s minds when they think of “The Strabanimal.” There was a collective euphoria across social media back then seeing the 21-year-old eat a side kick before getting pounded out, just a few minutes after being all up in Bandejas’s face. It’s the quintessential “chat s***, get banged” scenario playing out at a live sporting event. In fact, it’s such a classic of the genre, you’ll likely still see it pop up on your feed today, nearly a decade later. To simmer Gallagher’s career down to that one brutal defeat would be massively underselling the impact he had on the sport in his home country, though. As a teenager, Gallagher was like a mythological creature. Fighting grown men at age 13, it wasn’t until he was introduced to SBG head coach John Kavanagh that his dream began to take shape. His jiu-jitsu ability was the first thing most people heard about him. Experienced black belts would wax lyrical about his potential after his move to Dublin. Then, after blitzing through all the youth competitions, he began showing up at adult events and proving it wasn’t just hot air. James Gallagher and coach John Kavanaugh were a formidable duo early in Gallagher's MMA run. ASSOCIATED PRESS There was a buzz across the mats when Gallagher was competing. Early on he’d sport an oversized judo gi borrowed from a teammate and it looked like you could’ve fit three of him in there if it wasn’t for the blue belt keeping the outfit together. He’d smile, shake your hand, and more often than not he’d be on your back, using that same hand to apply a rear-naked choke a few seconds later. Eventually, Gallagher turned his focus to MMA. The hype began to grow around the Tyrone wonder kid as he treated the Irish amateur scene the same way he had the juvenile jiu-jitsu categories. He was the subject of mainstream media intrigue. The big publications had already been completely blindsided by the success of Conor McGregor, and they weren’t going to let that happen again. The plan was for Gallagher to take gold at the 2015 IMMAF World Championships in Las Vegas before going pro. A whole team of SBG amateurs ended up living at the Mac Mansion ahead of Conor McGregor’s interim title bid against Chad Mendes. The hysteria around McGregor led to the amateurs becoming commodities back home themselves, with Gallagher being the biggest point of intrigue on the back of the “next big thing” coverage carried across Ireland’s national publications. The IMMAF amateur world championships took place throughout the fight week leading up to UFC 189. Gallagher started strong, seeing off an American counterpart in

item.title: Nationals reliever Erik Tolman given the Tony Conigliaro award for his inspirational rise
item.description: WASHINGTON, DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA - SEPTEMBER 27, 2026: Erik Tolman #73 of the Washington Nationals pitches during the ninth inning of a game against the New York Mets at Nationals Park on September 27, 2026 in Washington, District of Columbia. The Nationals beat the Mets, 6-4. (Photo by Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Erik Tolman’s debut and success in the big leagues was one of the best stories in baseball during the 2026 season. The Nats left handed reliever had to overcome so many obstacles to get on to an MLB mound, but he did it. Today, Tolman was awarded with the Tony Conigliaro Award, which is given to a big leaguer who has overcome adversity. honoring erik 🙌 the Tony Conigliaro Award award recognizes a major leaguer who has overcome adversity through the attributes of spirit, determination, and courage. pic.twitter.com/uHrAbbMGzM — Washington Nationals (@Nationals) November 23, 2026 Conigliaro was a Red Sox player in the late 1960’s who was on the road to superstardom before getting hit in the face with a ball. That hit by pitch caused major damage, including some vision loss. Despite that, Conigliaro came back after missing a season. He put up quality numbers in 1969 and 1970, before the vision problems became so bad, he could not play anymore. The award has been handed out since 1990, and is usually given out to players who dealt with serious injuries or other health issues. Wilson Ramos is the only other National to win the award. He won it in 2014 due to coming back from injuries and a kidnapping. Tolman now joins him as a Nat to win the award. Tolman’s story is a ridiculous tale of perseverance. He had to undergo Tommy John twice in a short period of time after being drafted. That is bad enough, but these days that is not unheard of. However, in his return, Tolman tore up every ligament in his knee and more after his foot got stuck jumping over the foul line. This clip from Just Baseball does a good job explaining everything. MLB’s Story of the YEAR Erik Tolman of the Nationals comeback story is incredible pic.twitter.com/ee8hI3rVrZ — Just Baseball (@JustBB_Media) November 6, 2026 The biggest long term health problem from that injury was foot drop. Tolman is unable to move his foot side to side due to nerve damage. During that injury, his peroneal nerve was cut. So when Tolman is on the mound, he has to wear an ankle brace for stabilization. You can see his custom made brace when he is pitching. His story really resonated with me personally because I also have to wear a brace due to peroneal nerve damage. For me, the nerve got affected during a surgery to get a tumor removed. Tolman actually went to the same clinic to get his custom brace that I did. We talked about that and I wrote a story about Tolman and his brace. Erik Tolman and I both got AFO’s at the Hanger Clinic. His story sounded very familiar to me. However, his brace helped him become a lockdown reliever for the Nats https://t.co/j21cwKpNS6

item.title: Titans HC Robert Saleh shares candid ‘dogs---’ comment on recent play
item.description: Titans HC Robert Saleh shares candid ‘dogs---’ comment on recent play originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tennessee Titans are currently 1-9 on the season coming out of a Week 11 loss to the Dallas Cowboys , where the Tennessee defense couldn't stop Dak Prescott at any point during the game. After that recent loss, head coach Robert Saleh didn't mince his words when talking about whether the Titans are making any progress lately. Ari Meirov of The 33rd Team shared the viral quote from Saleh, with the Titans HC calling the last couple of weeks "dogs---" for Tennessee. HC Robert Saleh calls Titans' recent play 'dogs---' "But these last couple of weeks... I'm not going to try to sugarcoat anything: it's been dogs---," Saleh said. #Titans HC Robert Saleh on if there’s any progress being made: “These last couple of weeks. I'm not gonna try to sugarcoat anything. It's been dogshit." https://t.co/JjaGs9949G — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 23, 2026 It's quite the brutal quote from the Titans' head coach, but it's a candid response to some truly terrible defensive performances in recent weeks. Since beating the Indianapolis Colts back in Week 6, this Tennessee defense has been getting torched week in and week out. They allowed 27 points to the Cleveland Browns in a brutal loss, followed by allowing 43 points to the Cincinnati Bengals . They then had a Week 9 bye, followed by allowing 40 points in a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . MORE : Dak Prescott makes Cowboys history as Jerry Jones delivers telling reaction after Titans blowout Then, in a culmination of a horrible stretch these past four weeks, the Titans gave up 51 points to the Cowboys in another blowout loss. What's made this recent stretch so bad, and why Saleh's "dogs---" comment is warranted, is that Cam Ward and the Titans' offense have played well in that stretch, putting up 24, 36, 23, and 30 points since Week 7. The Titans are 1-9, sitting in last place in the AFC South, and are now set to face the Jaguars again in Week 12. After that, they get the Washington Commanders , Detroit Lions, Colts, Las Vegas Raiders , Pittsburgh Steelers , and Houston Texans . Saleh needs better play from his defense going forward, as the offense has made the necessary strides to be a competitive group week in and week out. The defense is just lagging, and to an extreme degree.
