item.title: NBA Power Rankings: Spurs And Knicks Are Clicking, Celtics Start Free-Falling
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images The NBA is shaping up nicely so far, and the latest standings have given us a much clearer picture of who’s legitimate and who’s starting to fall behind. The Los Angeles Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers are at the top of their respective conferences with identical 14-3 records, but the San Antonio Spurs might have the strongest overall statistical case in the league. The Spurs boast an impressive +11.50 SRS and one of the NBA’s best defenses, making them a serious threat to take the No. 1 spot. The New York Knicks are gaining momentum in the East, while the Minnesota Timberwolves , Houston Rockets , and Memphis Grizzlies are making the Western Conference very competitive. Meanwhile, Milwaukee’s disastrous 1-16 start and Utah’s continued struggles have sent both teams toward the bottom of the rankings. Let’s dive into the latest power rankings. 30. Milwaukee Bucks 2026-27 Record: 1-16, 15th in East Team Stats: 109.4 PPG, 121.7 OPPG, -10.71 SRS Milwaukee takes the last spot after an absolutely disastrous 1-16 start that has turned its season into an early crisis. The Bucks have won just once in 17 games, and their numbers offer very little encouragement. They’re averaging 109.4 points per game while allowing 121.7, exposing major problems on both ends of the floor. Whatever expectations Milwaukee entered the season with, this isn’t remotely close to what anyone envisioned. At this point, the Bucks need to find a way to stop the bleeding, and they might need Tyler Herro to continue dropping 50+ points to get there. 29. Sacramento Kings 2026-27 Record: 2-14, 15th in West Team Stats: 106.8 PPG, 119.1 OPPG, -8.71 SRS The Kings have fallen into a disastrous opening stretch, winning just twice in their first 16 games and sitting at the bottom of the Western Conference. They are averaging only 106.8 points per game while allowing 119.1, making their struggles painfully obvious on both ends. Right now, the Kings look like one of the NBA’s least competitive teams by a wide margin, with only the Bucks looking worse right now. At least the Kings are giving Darius Acuff Jr. a chance to get as many shots up as possible for a bid to try to “steal” the Rookie of the Year trophy for the year. That might be the only positive for the franchise at this point. 28. Brooklyn Nets 2026-27 Record: 3-12, 14th in East Team Stats: 110.9 PPG, 118.8 OPPG, -9.70 SRS Brooklyn has struggled to find any real momentum, winning just three of its first 15 games. The Nets have shown some offensive ability, averaging 110.9 points per contest, but their defense has been a significant problem. Allowing 118.8 points per game is a recipe for losing, especially when the offense isn’t consistently explosive enough to compensate. Brooklyn has a long way to go before it can be considered competitive with the Eastern Conference’s better teams, and considering how they have looked, it might be time to start cashing in on their veterans such as Julius Rand

item.title: Blue Jays Castoff Davis Schneider Breaks Silence After Cut
item.description: TORONTO, ON - JUNE 23: Davis Schneider #36 of the Toronto Blue Jays looks on from the dugout prior to a game against the Tampa Bay Rays at Rogers Centre on June 23, 2024 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Vaughn Ridley/Getty Images) Getty Images The Toronto Blue Jays launched their offseason changes with a few peripheral moves, including a harsh decision involving one of their more recognizable players. While the team’s offseason plans are only beginning to take shape, the sudden departure of longtime organizational favorite David Schneider resonated with the club’s fan base, following a near-decade long tenure with the franchise that included a notable career highlight during the World Series run in 2025. Now, shortly after the release, the former Blue Jays utility option offered his immediate thoughts on not being tenured a contract, effectively cutting him from the roster. “I spent nine-and-a half-years with the organization,” Schneider told Canadian baseball reporter Danny Gallagher . “Toronto is one of the greatest cities I could play for, in the whole country, in all of North America. It’s such a great fan base that wants you to succeed. Toronto fans are the best in the world.’’ FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Braves Reunite With Veteran Shortstop After Mauricio Dubon Exit Toronto Blue Jays Non-Tender Fan Favorite Davis Schneider After Long Tenure Schneider’s departure marked the end of a notable journey with Toronto, which selected him in the 28th round of the 2017 MLB Draft. Despite never emerging as a highly regarded prospect, he eventually worked his way to the major leagues and became a popular member of the organization. Then, last week, the team opted not to tender him a new contract. “Schneider, the moustachioed fan favourite who homered in his first big-league at-bat and later took Blake Snell deep to lead off Game 5 of the 2025 World Series, was non-tendered by the Blue Jays Friday evening,” Ben Nicholson-Smith reported for Sportsnet . “Money aside, there was likely less playing time for Schneider in an outfield also including Brett Bateman, Nathan Lukes, Addison Barger, Jonatan Clase and Anthony Santander. Utility players Josh Smith and Charles McAdoo further clouded the picture for Schneider, who’s now free to sign with any team.” The decision came as Schneider entered his first arbitration-eligible offseason. MLB Trade Rumors had projected him to earn approximately $1.3 million in 2027, but Toronto ultimately decided against bringing him back. His production had declined considerably in 2026. Schneider appeared in 69 games, hitting just .145 with five home runs and a .624 OPS. He finished his Blue Jays tenure with a .206/.322/.396 career batting line and 37 home runs across 978 plate appearances. item.title: GTA 6 radio mocks Jake Paul for boxing geezers, Paul responds
item.description: Jake Paul built his boxing career on the (bad) backs of boxing legends . When he’s not fighting geezers who s—t tar and use a wheelchair to get around , “El Gallo” is knocking around smaller MMA fighters who can’t box . Occasionally, Paul will venture outside his comfort zone, but those bouts typically end in decision losses and broken jaws . The makers of GTA 6 took notice. “In what promises to be a battle of the ages, former heavyweight boxing champion Tyler McNeil will re-enter the ring after nearly 50 years. McNeil will take on 22-year-old influencer Jacob Parker in a fight streaming live, who have assured subscribers that the 86-year-old’s dialysis machine will not hinder proceedings.” Paul responded on X: “As a kid I played GTA all the time and listened to the radio while driving for hours,” Paul wrote . “Never thought I’d be joked about in the biggest entertainment product of all time. The younger me is smiling.” Paul, 29, returns to the ring to box the older, smaller Cédric Doumbé on Christmas Eve in Dubai.

item.title: Former MVP Goldschmidt Brings More Pop to the Mets
item.description: Aug 28, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees first baseman Paul Goldschmidt (48) at bat against the Boston Red Sox during the sixth inning at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tom Horak-Imagn Images A day after locking up Tarik Skubal, the New York Mets continued their aggressive offseason by agreeing to terms with veteran first baseman Paul Goldschmidt. The deal is for one year and $8 million , with the chance to earn up to $2 million more in performance bonuses, according to multiple reports. The 39-year-old Goldschmidt spent the past two seasons with the Yankees and now makes the short trip across town. In 2026, he hit .252/.313/.452 with 18 home runs and 52 RBIs in 105 games. His real value came against left-handed pitching, where he posted a .967 OPS with 11 home runs. He also graded as an above-average defender at first base. Two future Hall of Famers in two days for Mets. Goldschmidt fits Mets as platoon at 1B with Jared Young. $8M plus incentives for Goldy, via @Joelsherman1 https://t.co/NlD0Kts595 — Jon Heyman (@JonHeyman) November 23, 2026 For the Mets, the signing addresses a clear need . After Pete Alonso left for Baltimore, first base was a weak spot in 2026. Goldschmidt is expected to form a platoon with left-handed hitter Jared Young, giving New York a proven right-handed bat who still mashes southpaws while providing solid defense and veteran leadership. Goldschmidt is a seven-time All-Star, four-time Gold Glove winner, and the 2022 National League MVP. Even at this stage of his career, he remains a productive role player rather than an everyday force. item.title: Commanders Week 11 injury report vs. Bengals for MNF: 4 players listed as questionable
item.description: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Commanders Week 11 injury report vs. Bengals for MNF: 4 players listed as questionable appeared first on ClutchPoints . It’s a game that gives Washington a chance to earn its fourth win of the season, after going 3-5-1 to begin the campaign. However, the team is dealing with several injuries on the roster, with four players deemed questionable going into the contest. Here’s everything we know about those four players, and more. Croskey-Merritt has not played since the club’s 27-27 overtime tie with the New York Giants in Week 5. Washington just recently activated Croskey-Merritt from the IR in the week leading up to the game against the Bengals. This season, he’s accumulated 239 yards and two touchdowns on 67 rush attempts. At the very least, Jayden Daniels has been playing well since returning from his elbow injury. But Washington will still want its players healthy against Cincinnati. item.title: What Warriors forward Draymond Green simply doesn’t ‘understand’ about massive GTA 6 hype
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images What Warriors forward Draymond Green simply doesn’t ‘understand’ about massive GTA 6 hype appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green isn’t buying into the massive excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto VI. While the Warriors veteran regularly shares his opinions , he admits he struggles to understand why some people would miss work just to play a video game. Green reacted to the GTA 6 craze , explaining that video games have never been a major part of his life. His latest discussion took him away from basketball and into the gaming world. “I’m not a video game player myself. I think the last GTA I remember playing is like San Andreas,” Green admitted. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite his limited gaming experience, Green acknowledged the enormous attention surrounding Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated release. “The excitement level, it’s unbelievable,” he said. However, one particular aspect of the anticipation left the four-time NBA champion completely puzzled. “I don’t understand people calling out of work to play a video game,” Green explained. Still, Green made it clear that he wasn’t criticizing anyone for enjoying something he personally doesn’t follow. “To all you GTAers out there, kudos to you. Much respect, much love. Your thing is your thing,” he said. Green’s reaction reflects his unfamiliarity with modern gaming culture rather than opposition to the franchise itself. The outspoken forward has never shied away from sharing his perspective , whether discussing basketball controversies or topics outside the NBA. For GTA 6 fans, taking time off to play might sound reasonable. For Green, however, the excitement remains something he can appreciate without fully understanding. His comments also highlight how differently people approach gaming today. item.title: APC’ll win three South-East states; Obi will take Abia, Anambra — Bwala
item.description: The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has projected that the All Progressives Congress will win three states in the South-East in the 2027 general elections, while conceding that Peter Obi could retain a stronghold in Abia and Anambra. Bwala made the projection during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief on Monday, where he was asked how the ruling party intended to secure victories in the region. He said Obi’s popularity in the two states could make them difficult for the APC to win, but expressed confidence that the party would prevail in the remaining South-East states. “We will struggle in Abia. You see, in Abia and Anambra, Peter has a very convincing presence. Even in these two states, I am assuming that if we lose, we still come second, which is not a bad thing. Apart from these two states, the remainder of the states, we are winning,” Bwala said. The presidential aide, however, stressed that his assessment was a projection rather than a definitive prediction, noting that different political actors could arrive at varying conclusions from available data. He said the party was willing to acknowledge areas where it might face difficulties rather than make sweeping claims about its chances. “Where we think we may not, and I use the word advisedly because none of what I’m saying is cast in stone, right? It is projection, and two people from the same political party can have different projections based on our own interpretation of data,” he said. Bwala added that admitting potential weaknesses was more honest than claiming the APC would win everywhere, noting that his use of the word “struggle” referred specifically to the party’s chances of winning those states. The presidential adviser also expressed confidence in the APC’s overall prospects ahead of the 2027 elections, dismissing the opposition’s preparedness to challenge the ruling party. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” he said. item.title: FG seeks 18-month completion period for new Carter Bridge
item.description: The Federal Government is seeking reduction in the period for construction of the new Carter Bridge. The Minister of Works, Sen. Dave Umahi, told the contractor handling the project, China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC), to look at the possibility of reducing the time frame from 36 months to 18 months or 24 months. He said that the aim was to save more money and ensure that the new Carter Bridge would come on board before the existing one would go down. He said that CCECC had completed five per cent of the 1.9km bridge project without being paid any mobilisation fee. “No mobilisation fee has been paid to them, and the duration of this project is 36 months but I am striking a deal with their management, having seen that they have gone up to five per cent. “We are going to release, within this week, 30 per cent mobilisation fee to CCECC. “Another deal will probably be if we can reduce the construction period to about 18 months to 24 months; then, they can apply for loan so they can set up two other sections of piling. ” if they will do that, we are ready to give them a loan of 20 per cent so that they can set up, but they must give us APG – Advance Payment Guarantee,” the minister said. According to him, the Federal Government already has the APG for the 30 per cent mobilisation fee. “We are not allowed to pay more than 30 per cent but we can give a loan based on an agreement.” He emphasised that the bridge’s piling must be on a minimum of Schedule 60 thick steel pile. He said that the CCECC was meeting the specification. “We are very happy about that. We also directed that when they start their piling, we have to do a number of big lumps to protect the piles at the seabed,” Umahi said The post FG seeks 18-month completion period for new Carter Bridge appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Holding election with disputed voters’ register amounts to rigging – APM
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has warned that conducting the 2027 general elections with a disputed voters’ register would amount to rigging, accusing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of creating room for electoral manipulation by postponing its clean-up until after the polls. The party said the decision could undermine confidence in the electoral process, warning that unresolved concerns over the register could compromise the credibility of the 2027 elections. Responding to Vanguard’s enquiry on INEC’s decision, APM National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, described the postponement as another form of electoral manipulation and vowed that the party would resist any attempt to subvert the will of voters. “That’s another form of rigging the 2027 elections. Going into an election with a controversial register is tantamount to rigging, just like we had the case of electronic voting and BVAS,” Yusuf said. Citing the Kogi Central senatorial district election, Yusuf alleged that the experience showed how electoral outcomes could be manipulated in favour of the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. “You remember in Kogi Central, election results were written by APC and the candidate declared as governor. I think that’s what they are going to adopt this time around,” he alleged. He insisted that APM would not accept any attempt to compromise the electoral process, declaring that the party would join other opposition groups to resist interference with voters’ choices. “APM will not succumb to INEC gimmicks. Any attempt to rig or tamper with the judgement of Nigerians in the forthcoming general elections will be resisted by not only APM, but opposition parties,” he said. Yusuf urged INEC to put its electoral preparations in order, warning against any action capable of compromising the 2027 elections. “INEC must do the needful by putting everything in order,” he added. The post 2027: Holding election with disputed voters’ register amounts to rigging – APM appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ghana defeat Morocco to win maiden Amputee Football World Cup title
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have emerged champions of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup after defeating Morocco 1-0 in the final held in Mexico. The victory marks Ghana’s first title in the competition and a historic achievement for the country’s football. The decisive goal came from a free-kick by Mubarik Mohammed, whose effort led to an own goal by Morocco, giving the Black Challenge the advantage they held until the final whistle. Mohammed also finished the tournament as its highest goalscorer, finding the net seven times during Ghana’s impressive campaign. The Black Challenge had earlier secured their place in the final after defeating defending champions Turkey on penalties in the semi-finals. They also recorded a 2-0 victory over Egypt to book their place in the last four. The triumph over Morocco brings Ghana’s successful campaign to a fitting end and earns the team its first world title in amputee football. item.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network. The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed. How the solo block played out The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000. Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.” He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote. The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node. A recent run of solo wins Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page . The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC. Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC. Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee. Network hashrate and difficulty Bitcoin’s network hashrate was about 1.04 zettahashes per second, or roughly 1,043 exahashes, on a three-day average Monday. At 11.1 TH/s, the winning miner contributes about 0.000001% of that total, which fits Kolivas’s odds. One in 1,650 works out to a chance of about 0.06% over a full year of mining. Mining difficulty is about 134.8 trillion. The last adjustment cut it by about 9.1%, and the next one, expected around Nov. 26, is estimated to raise it by about 9.2%, according to mempool.space. Difficulty resets every 2,016 blocks to keep blocks ar

item.title: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
item.description: Artist’s concept of a nuclear fission power system on the Moon’s surface. Credit: NASA NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface. Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For NASA’s plans for a Moon Base , that energy could support future habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments, and other essential infrastructure. NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment. Unlike solar power, which depends on sunlight, a nuclear reactor can generate electricity continuously, including during the Moon’s approximately two-week-long nights. This capability will enable future lunar operations, particularly in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable. “This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager. “A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface. Space nuclear systems will provide continuous power to NASA assets in any environment without dependency on sunlight.” NASA’s Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback received after the agency released a draft proposal in August and hosted an industry day in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The solicitation requires that the reactor must meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations. While the primary purpose of the Request for Proposals is to advance the technology, testing, and flight design of LR-1, NASA may issue additional task orders to support the development of other space nuclear power systems. Proposals are due by Dec. 21. Nuclear power will be increasingly important to NASA’s space exploration ambitions. Lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months. Farther from the Sun, solar power becomes progressively less effective. Nuclear systems offer a reliable source of electricity in these challenging environments. LR-1 is managed by the agency’s Space Reactors Division in partnership with the Department of Energy. The division is also responsible for the development of NASA’s Space Reactor‑1 (SR-1) Freedom. Scheduled to launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom will deliver three SkyFall helicopters to Mars and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion, which uses electricity generated by a nuclear reactor to power spacecraft propulsion systems. This technology could enable future spacecraft to travel farther and undertake deep space missions that aren’t pos

item.title: Bulgaria evicts cyber snoops who lurked inside government networks for 5 years
item.description: The Ancient Thracian heartland of Bulgaria says it has shut down a cyberespionage operation that gave intruders access to government networks for five years – the longest-running known campaign against its administration. Bulgaria's Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation said the unauthorized and officially unattributed attackers first gained access to infrastructure used by government institutions to exchange information in 2021. It explained that the intrusion went unnoticed for so long because "the previous means of protection did not work as a single, integrated system," and that without a new, recently installed product, it may have gone undetected for much longer. "The incident was discovered thanks to the new national cybersecurity system, which for the first time provides a single picture of what is happening in state networks," the ministry added. "Without it, this activity would most likely have remained hidden for an indefinite period of time." Bulgaria acknowledged that "sensitive information related to the work of the state" was accessed, but did not specify the scale of the compromise. Innovation and Digital Transformation Minister Ivan Vasilev said attackers had downloaded more than 130 GB of data over five years. He also put the volume at 62 million pages. The Register contacted the Bulgarian government for confirmation of these numbers. The ministry said that it has not yet found any evidence that citizens' personal data was compromised, and that the affected infrastructure "will be under increased surveillance for 90 days" in case the attackers try to regain access. Vasilev said multiple international hacking groups had accessed government systems since 2021. He did not specify the names of these groups, however, nor did he name any specific countries that may have been involved. In a follow-up interview with bTV , Vasilev blamed political instability and frequent changes of ministerial leadership for leaving government systems inadequately protected. A representative of the Progressive Bulgaria party, which back in May won Bulgaria's eighth general election in five years, Vasilev said the "constant change of leadership" means "important things for the state do not actually happen." Vasilev said the intrusion was discovered over the summer as the national cybersecurity system was upgraded, and that teams had spent the past three to four months removing the attackers. ®

item.title: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance
item.description: null NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life. NASA's Curiosity rover recently wrapped up a drilling campaign at a location nicknamed "Nazca," where scientists have been examining unusual disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. Some of the features are so thin and flat that the mission team likened them to potato chips, according to a statement from the space agency. NASA's Curiosity rover captured a close-up view of unusual, disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in Martian bedrock using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) on Nov. 7, 2026 (Sol 5067). The thin, flattened formations resemble tiny potato chips. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) Curiosity used its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), mounted on the end of its robotic arm, to capture detailed close-up images of the formations on Nov. 7 — the rover's 5,067th Martian day , or Sol 5067. The rover also used its ChemCam instrument to study the rocks' chemical composition, while samples from the Nazca drill site were delivered to its onboard Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) instrument for further analysis. Meanwhile, NASA's Perseverance rover has been investigating a collection of unusually bright rocks in an area called "Idubi," located in the “Lac de Charmes” region outside Jezero Crater. The rover captured images of the formations on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), revealing pale, ghostly-looking rocks that stand out dramatically against the darker, dust-covered Martian landscape. Data from Perseverance's SuperCam instrument revealed that the rocks are rich in hydrated silica rather than being typical igneous rocks. That discovery has scientists particularly interested. On Earth, hydrated silica can form in environments involving hydrothermal activity or groundwater. These deposits are also capable of preserving microscopic fossils, making them valuable targets in the search for evidence of ancient life, according to another statement from NASA. NASA's Perseverance rover captured unusually bright, silica-rich rock in the "Idubi" area outside Jezero Crater on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), using its left Mastcam-Z camera. The pale formation stands out against the darker, dust-covered Martian terrain. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU) Perseverance is now conducting a closer investigation of the formations, using its instruments to gather detailed chemical and mineralogical data that could help scient

item.title: Reps fault states over poor support for small businesses
item.description: …Propose N1bn monthly MSME fund per state, condemn high lending rates, red tape By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has faulted state governments for failing to adequately support small businesses despite increased federal allocations, proposing a minimum monthly intervention fund of N1bn in each state to boost Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, said state governments had the financial capacity to establish dedicated funds for entrepreneurs but had not demonstrated sufficient commitment to supporting grassroots economic development. Abbas, who spoke on Monday through the House Majority Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, at a stakeholders’ engagement organised by the House Committee on Small and Medium Enterprises in Abuja, said the survival of many small businesses depended largely on the resilience of their owners rather than meaningful government support. He argued that state and local governments must take greater responsibility for creating economic opportunities, stressing that the Federal Government alone could not address the country’s economic challenges. “There is no governor in this country that cannot put one billion a month in a special fund for MSMEs in his state. There is no state that cannot do it,” he said. The Speaker lamented that entrepreneurs who had managed to survive Nigeria’s difficult business environment were doing so largely without meaningful assistance from government institutions and intervention agencies. “Those that are surviving are surviving not because of government and agencies, but in spite of government and agencies,” Abbas said. He also criticised the bureaucratic procedures attached to accessing government intervention funds, arguing that excessive administrative requirements had undermined the effectiveness of programmes designed to support small businesses. “I’m a systems man, but I know this system is not working. And it will not work when you bureaucratise a procedure. A lot of red tape,” he said. Abbas further condemned high lending rates, warning that double-digit interest rates were inimical to the growth of small businesses. He said entrepreneurs needed affordable and flexible financing arrangements that would allow their businesses to stabilise and generate returns before repayment obligations became due. The Speaker urged state governors to establish transparent funding mechanisms, with effective monitoring and clearly defined eligibility criteria, to ensure that genuine entrepreneurs, particularly those operating at the grassroots, benefited from the proposed interventions. He also called on Nigerians to hold elected officials accountable at all levels, noting that the performance of state and local governments had direct implications for employment generation and economic prosperity. item.title: Sowore slams presidential candidates for leaving youths to fight electoral injustice
item.description: Human rights activist and former presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, has criticised opposition presidential hopefuls for allegedly leaving Nigerian youths to confront electoral injustice and repression while they position themselves to benefit from the outcome of the struggle. Sowore said politicians seeking to take advantage of demands for credible elections should also be willing to participate in protests and make sacrifices rather than leave the burden to ordinary Nigerians. In a post on X, he lamented that young Nigerians were expected to take to the streets and confront electoral manipulation while presidential candidates remained detached from the struggle. “Shame on presidential candidates who expect Nigerian youths to take to the streets, confront electoral injustice, endure repression, and make all the sacrifices, while they sit comfortably on the sidelines, waiting to reap the benefits of free and fair elections without lifting a finger!” he wrote. The activist made the remarks following his participation in a protest against electoral violence and manipulation at the headquarters of the Independent National Electoral Commission in Abuja. In an earlier post recounting the demonstration, Sowore said protesters chanted slogans demanding President Bola Tinubu’s removal as he arrived at the commission’s headquarters. He accused some opposition politicians of focusing on political negotiations and power-sharing arrangements instead of joining citizens to challenge what he described as electoral injustice. “While ordinary Nigerians confront the system on the streets, these politicians remain tucked away in cozy conference rooms, negotiating who gets what and who will control Nigeria’s resources if they eventually capture power,” he said. Sowore argued that political leaders should not expect to benefit from the sacrifices of citizens without contributing to the struggle for democratic accountability. “You cannot outsource the struggle for liberation and expect to inherit its rewards!” he declared. His comments come amid renewed political activities and debates over electoral credibility, political participation and opposition strategies ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post Sowore slams presidential candidates for leaving youths to fight electoral injustice appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FIFA names UK as 2035 Women’s World Cup host
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will jointly host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup, while Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico and the United States will stage the 2031 tournament. According to Sky Sports, the UK bid was unopposed after FIFA declared it the only valid bid in April 2025. FIFA’s Congress ratified the bid on Monday, alongside the joint proposal from Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico and the US to host the 2031 competition. The 2035 tournament will be the first football World Cup held in the UK since the men’s competition in 1966. It is set to feature 48 teams and 104 matches over 39 days. FIFA has yet to confirm the dates or whether all four host nations will qualify automatically. The UK’s “All Together” bid proposed 19 stadiums across 15 cities: 14 in England, two in Scotland, two in Wales and one in Northern Ireland. Three additional venues — in Birmingham, Wrexham and a proposed new Chelsea stadium — could be added, taking the tournament to 22 stadiums across 16 cities. Presenting the UK bid, Sky Sports News presenter Jess Creighton said its ambition was to deliver “the most-watched FIFA Women’s World Cup ever”, predicting more than 3.5 billion viewers and over 4.5 million tickets sold. The 2031 edition will be the first Women’s World Cup contested by 48 teams. The four countries’ bid also ran unopposed before FIFA approved it. The post FIFA names UK as 2035 Women’s World Cup host appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [PHOTOS] FG Targets December For Reopening Of Eko, Iddo Bridges
item.description: The Federal Government has assured Lagos residents that the Eko and Iddo bridges will be fully functional by December 2026, as rehabilitation and reconstruction works continue on the two critical transport links. The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, gave the assurance during an inspection of the ongoing projects in Lagos, where he assessed the progress of work and commended the quality of interventions being carried out. This image shows ongoing reconstruction of the Iddo Bridge in Lagos. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) At Eko Bridge, rehabilitation works were focused on addressing concerns surrounding some of its supporting structural components, while Iddo Bridge is undergoing reconstruction. Umahi expressed satisfaction with the progress recorded at both sites, assuring that the contractors would deliver the projects within the December deadline. “We are satisfied with what they’re doing. They are very fast in what they’re doing. They have good knowledge of what they are doing. And so we — as Ministry of Works — we are very satisfied,” the minister said. “And they promised us that by December, they will definitely complete the job and the full integrity of the bridge will be restored.” This image shows ongoing reconstruction of the Iddo Bridge in Lagos. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) The inspection forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to restore the two important infrastructure links, which serve thousands of commuters and businesses across Lagos. The ongoing construction activities have continued to affect movement around the affected corridors, with motorists and commuters having to contend with traffic disruptions. Umahi (2nd-left) commended the level of work done on the projects so far. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) The minister’s assurance comes amid expectations that completing the projects will improve connectivity, ease traffic congestion, and enhance the safety of road users. Attention will now be on the contractors’ ability to meet the December deadline while ensuring that the restored infrastructure meets the required structural and safety standards. item.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
item.description: Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures. The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer. A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments. The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14. Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost. The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix. Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising. Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom. Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing. Microsoft also plans to improve diagnostics and change auditing so engineers can identify troublesome Windows changes faster. July's defect had been running worldwide for more than three months before it brought the gateways down. ®

item.title: Marvel crams every superhero ever into Avengers: Doomsday final trailer

As previously reported , the film takes place 14 months after the events of Thunderbolts* . Per the official logline: “Beloved heroes from three distinct universes will be set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever encountered.” Those universes are Earth-616 (the Avengers, Wakandans, and New Avengers), Earth-828 (Fantastic Four), and the “original” X-Men. Cast-wise, we have Avengers favorites Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the new Captain America (Anthony Mackie), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Falcon (Danny Ramirez), and Loki (Tom Hiddleston). Then there’s the Wakandan contingent: Shuri as the new Black Panther (Letitia Wright), M’Baku (Winston Duke), and Namor (Tenoch Huerta Mejia), as well as Alex Livinalli as Namor’s ally, Attuma. item.title: Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares Nvidia shares jumped about 35% on Monday after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, restoring roughly $1 trillion in market value at the open. The stock traded near $169.20 at 10:41 a.m. ET, up from Friday’s close of $125.53, and Wall Street rallied with it. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back, effective immediately, after what it called a series of discussions and meetings. It said it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and is confident his return “poses no national security risk.” President Donald Trump had urged the move. Several items remain open. An independent board committee will finish its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and Huang said he will cooperate. Nvidia also formed a national security and export control committee and is searching for a chief compliance officer. From resignation to reversal Huang resigned on Nov. 11, days after admitting an affair with a woman U.S. officials believe is linked to Chinese intelligence. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey Jones became board chair. Nvidia had said it was searching for a permanent successor. The stock slid for seven straight weeks, the longest such streak since 2008. On Friday it plunged 14% after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining the company’s accounting practices. Reuters noted that investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing. Huang’s return reverses most of the losses since his affair became public. The selloff came even after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly results on Nov. 17. For weeks, the board had said it was not considering bringing Huang back, which makes Monday’s announcement a sharp turn for the world’s most closely watched chipmaker. Wall Street and chip stocks rally The Nasdaq Composite rose about 7.4% to near 24,300 at 10:41 a.m. ET, and the S&P 500 gained about 5.4% to near 7,280. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed about 3.3%, or more than 1,500 points, to near 49,700. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days. Chip stocks followed Nvidia higher. Micron (MU) rose about 21% and Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) gained about 16%, while Intel (INTC) added about 15%. AMD rose about 9% and Broadcom (AVGO) was up about 3%. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned on Sunday that the Fed may be making a “policy mistake” if it overtightens. The central bank meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point increase remains the base case. Bitcoin and crypto stocks follow The bitcoin price climbed to a Monday high near $64,500, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, and was near $63,000 at 10:41 a.m. ET. That is about $8,000 above the weekend low of $55,106, hit at roughly 1:17 a.m. ET on Saturday. Bitcoin had slid with stocks on Friday. Crypto-linked stocks jumped. item.title: Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA Cross River Bank has launched its first bitcoin-backed loans, working with consumer lender LendingUSA to let eligible borrowers take out between $10,000 and $250,000 against their BTC without selling it. The program is the first time Cross River has originated bitcoin-secured loans itself, according to The Block. LendingUSA runs the application platform, and every loan is made by Cross River, a New Jersey state-chartered bank, according to LendingUSA . How the loans work Borrowers can choose a loan-to-value ratio of 30%, 50% or 70%, which sets how much cash they receive against the value of the bitcoin they pledge. LendingUSA defines the ratio as the loan balance divided by the value of the collateral, so a 50% loan against $100,000 of bitcoin would be $50,000. Two repayment options are offered: interest-only or no monthly payments. On an interest-only loan, borrowers make smaller monthly payments that roughly cover interest, with the principal and any remaining interest due at the end of the term. On a no-monthly-payment loan, the full balance plus interest is due at the end. LendingUSA says borrowers can repay early without penalties or fees . Applicants go through a soft credit check, and LendingUSA says approval rests on the crypto being pledged rather than a credit score. The company says funding typically arrives within one to three business days after the collateral is verified. Custody and margin risk A qualified third-party custodian holds the bitcoin for the life of the loan. Once the loan is repaid in full, the collateral is released back to the borrower, according to the company. The terms carry the usual risk of borrowing against a volatile asset. LendingUSA says that if the value of the bitcoin falls, the loan-to-value ratio rises, and borrowers may be asked to add collateral or pay down the debt to avoid liquidation. The company says it will try to notify borrowers first but cannot guarantee it during fast price moves. The timing matters. Bitcoin was trading near $61,000 on Monday morning, so a borrower at the 70% tier would have far less room before a collateral call than one at the 30% tier. Lower ratios leave a bigger cushion but unlock less cash per bitcoin pledged. LendingUSA markets the loans for uses such as debt consolidation, home improvements and large purchases. The company says it has served more than 200,000 borrowers across its lending business, and the crypto product is its first expansion into digital asset-backed loans. A chartered bank joins bitcoin lending Cross River President Evan Russo framed the launch as a natural extension of the bank’s work. “Digital assets have become a meaningful part of how many consumers build and hold wealth, and the financial system must evolve to serve them responsibly,” Russo said in a statement. “Cross River was built on the belief that innovation and trusted infrastructure go hand in hand,”

item.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' gets final trailer, explaining why Steve Rogers is back and showing an epic battle with the X-Men
item.description: The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday just landed, and it finally puts the spotlight on our boy Steve Rogers. Avengers: Doomsday has been promising the scale and excitement the MCU has often been lacking since the Infinity Saga. Previous trailers played it safe, mostly setting up the conflict and introducing Victor Von Doom. Now it’s time for one last explosive look at the film before it tries to conquer cinemas next month. Disney and Marvel Studios have just released a "final trailer" that puts the focus back on Steve Rogers — no longer Captain America but still ready to use Mjolnir — and Thor as the veterans leading the New Avengers, former colleagues, the Fantastic Four, and even Fox's X-Men (after some first-encounter fights, of course) against Doom and his followers. A few dodgy CG shots aside, it looks grand, and if you're a big X-Men fan, it's hard not to get goosebumps when Cyclops (James Marsden) finally gets to say the thing. The multiverse-spanning story is still largely kept a secret in this trailer, but at least we get a better sense of what the emotional stakes are for Rogers and how all these heroes can realistically work together against the greatest threat they've faced so far (even if most of them won't get more than a few lines). (Image credit: Marvel) As for Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, this isn't his trailer, but the mysterious Latverian witches — who have fueled many theories online for months — are finally seen in motion. Doom has, however, received a simple but evocative poster that mirrors one of the original Iron Man ones. Even though Marvel Studios' honcho, Kevin Feige, has shot down the theory that this Victor Von Doom is a Tony Stark variant , you can't stop marketing from doing the obvious things, it seems. We won't complain. (Image credit: Marvel Studios) Avengers: Doomsday won't fix all of the Multiverse Saga's shortcomings, but at the very least, it looks like a proper fun time with more toys being mashed together than ever before and proper stakes. Right before Christmas, it's hard to resist such a pitch. Avengers: Doomsday assembles on December 18, 2026, only in cinemas...Yes, it opens the same day as Dune: Part Three . item.title: British retailer Next downplays data breach at tech supplier
item.description: British retailer Next has become the latest high street name to find itself caught up in a cyberattack, although it insists the data accessed by hackers is "benign" and its customers have nothing to worry about. The clothing and homeware giant told investors on Monday that a third-party supplier had suffered a security breach, allowing an unauthorized party to access information relating to Next. The retailer says its own systems remain untouched and that, so far, there's no evidence that customer personal data has fallen into the wrong hands. "We have been informed that one of our third-party online suppliers has experienced a cyber incident which has resulted in unauthorized access to certain benign data relating to NEXT," the company said in its statement, which it shared with The Register . "We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier." The breached supplier provides technology services to Next, and the "benign" information accessed is understood to be low-level data. Sensitive customer details, including addresses, passwords, and banking information, are believed to be unaffected. Next hasn't identified the supplier, explained exactly what the hackers managed to get their hands on, or revealed how much information was accessed, and declined to say when asked by The Register . However, the retailer has seemingly decided that the stolen data won’t be of much use to the criminals responsible. "Our investigations are ongoing; however, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised," Next said. "The information affected is limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or NEXT." Next also stressed that its own IT infrastructure had escaped unscathed, saying it was "confident that NEXT’s own systems have not been compromised and that this remains an incident affecting the supplier's environment." Despite repeatedly describing the compromised information as harmless, Next says it is treating the incident "with the utmost seriousness" and is working with the affected supplier, law enforcement, and relevant regulators. The incident comes just weeks after fellow British fashion retailer Asos suffered a breach of its own , with hackers gaining access to customer information through third-party platforms. That attack, which came to light on October 6 when customers received an unauthorized push notification through the Asos app announcing that the company had been hacked, was traced to a social engineering scam. An attacker impersonated a trusted contact to trick an Asos employee into handing over login credentials, which were then used to access external platforms. Asos later admitted that the intruders had accessed customer names, contact details, and some account information, but passwords and payment card details were apparently off limits. item.description: Explore Webb Science James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) NASA’s Webb Shows How… Webb News Latest News Latest Images Webb’s Blog Awards X (offsite – login reqd) Instagram (offsite – login reqd) Facebook (offsite- login reqd) Youtube (offsite) Overview About Who is James Webb? The composition of its dust provides clues to the structure of Cassiopeia A’s original star. Credits: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Columbia), Rick Arendt (UMBC), Dan Milisavljevic (Purdue University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets. This high-resolution, mid-infrared observation from Webb reveals new details that are helping astronomers chronicle the structure and evolution of Cas A’s original star. The Webb data supports a scenario in which the interior of the star underwent a dramatic change, possibly just hours before its demise. These results published Monday in The Astrophysical Journal Letters . Image: Dust In Cassiopeia A (MIRI Image) NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals the hot dust that makes up Cassiopeia A. The composition of its dust provides clues to the structure of Cassiopeia A’s original star. Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Columbia University), Rick Arendt (UMBC), Dan Milisavljevic (Purdue University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) Stars begin their lives as large clouds of mostly hydrogen gas and cosmic dust called molecular clouds. Eventually, gravity causes these molecular clouds to collapse, the material heats up, and protostars — infant stars — form. Under the constant pressure of gravity, hydrogen within a protostar begins to fuse into helium, which marks the point where protostars evolve into full-fledged stars like our Sun. As hydrogen in the core runs out, the core contracts and heats until helium begins to fuse into heavier elements. This process repeats as stars like Cas A’s original star evolve

item.title: The remains of a long-dead volcano on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 23, 2026
item.description: null An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

item.title: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed and patched a medium-severity bug that let an attacker temporarily freeze a node’s processing of blocks and transactions, a flaw first flagged by an AI scanner built by Block’s Spiral. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, is fixed in Bitcoin Core versions 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1. The 30.5 and 31.3 releases shipped Friday alongside the public advisory, while 32.1 has carried the fix since Oct. 27. Affected versions run from 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4 and 31.0 through 31.2. The 29.x series has reached end of life and will not get a fix, so operators on that branch need to move to a newer release. How the Core bug worked Bitcoin Core keeps “orphan” transactions, whose parent transactions it has not yet seen, and asks peers that announce them for the missing pieces. Since version 29.0, the software builds a list of an orphan’s parents and checks each one against its mempool and filters before deciding what to request. A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and the software did not skip duplicates. An attacker could send a node an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then send messages repeating that transaction’s ID 50,000 times. “Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks,” the advisory said. Sending more messages could stretch the disruption out. The fix makes the node process each transaction announced in an inv message only once. The advisory describes a temporary denial-of-service problem and does not describe any way to steal bitcoin or permanently damage a node. It also does not say whether the bug was ever exploited. For a business running an affected node, the stalls could still matter. An exchange could be slow to credit deposits, and a miner could keep working on an outdated view of the chain while its node is stuck. An AI-found bug under a faster disclosure policy The advisory credits an automated LLM scan run through Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral, Block’s open-source bitcoin development arm. Bitcoin Core developer Gregory Sanders validated the finding and brought it to the project’s security team. Loupe is a free scanner that runs AI agents over open-source bitcoin code and only reports findings backed by a working test case. Bitcoin Core, BDK, LDK, rust-bitcoin, Cashu, Blockstream Jade, bitcoinj and SRI signed up for its first round of scans. Rohrer said on a recent podcast that Spiral started the project around March and began continuous scanning in May, with Bitcoin Core in the first batch. Loupe reported the issue on July 8. A developer known as Stutxo independently reported it on Aug. 4, the same day Sanders opened a pull request with the fix, which was merged two days later. The fix was backported to the 30.x and 31.x branches on Nov. 17. Bitcoin Core rated the bug “easily discovera

item.title: Nvidia board puts Jensen Huang back as boss
item.description: There's no telling what caused the Nvidia board to unanimously vote to reinstate Huang less than a week after saying his return wasn’t under consideration - except reportedly the threat of having one's head ripped off and brain peed on - but that really doesn't matter, at least as far as shareholders need to be concerned: Jensen's back in charge and all’s right in the world of chip stocks. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said of the decision to reinstate him, calling it an honor. Nvidia kicked its former-cum-current CEO and president to the curb on November 12, but not over allegations that he may have been sleeping with a suspected Chinese spy - it was affairs at Nvidia with his subordinates that appears to have been the last straw with Nvidia directors. Nvidia stock has tumbled since Huang’s ouster, and much of the rest of the tech stock world followed suit . Nvidia insiders and tech heavyweights have been pushing for Huang’s return for about as long as he was unemployed, but calls for his return from the US federal government may have been the catalyst for a change of heart among Nvidia leadership who didn’t want Huang back. "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk," Nvidia said in its statement announcing Huang’s return. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," board chair Harvey Jones added. Jones was made Nvidia's first board chair upon Huang’s resignation, and will remain in that role. The White House has since confirmed that the senior-level official involved in Huang’s reinstatement was President Trump. According to a White House statement to Semafor, Trump personally dialed in to an Nvidia board meeting hours before Huang was reinstated to argue for his return. “President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board,” White House comms director Steven Cheung told Semafor. “We have to protect our geniuses.” "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security," Trump said in a post on Truth Social. "The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." ® Updated at 1607 to include the fact that Trump dialed into a board meeting.

item.title: Bitcoin Price Surges Above $64,000 as Nvidia Reinstates CEO
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Surges Above $64,000 as Nvidia Reinstates CEO The bitcoin price surged to above $64,000 on Monday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive and sent stocks sharply higher. Bitcoin is up about $8,500 from its weekend low of roughly $55,100, which came at about 1:17 a.m. ET on Saturday. Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, the company said Monday morning. The board said it spoke with Huang and received input from “senior levels of the United States government,” concluding that his return “poses no national security risk.” Nvidia board restores Huang after 12 days Huang resigned on Nov. 11 after reports of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress took over as interim CEO. The board has said an investigation into the reported foreign intelligence effort will continue, and Huang said he supports it. Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said the board believes Huang “is the right person to lead” the company. Huang called it an honor to return and said he “can’t wait to get back to work.” The company also formed a national security and export control committee and is searching for a chief compliance officer. The stock had lost nearly half its value during a seven-week losing streak, even after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly results on Nov. 17. Investors worried about life without Huang, and bitcoin traded in step with the rout in technology shares. Nvidia (NVDA) shares were up roughly 31% to near $165 in premarket trading. Shares had tumbled 14% on Friday, closing out that seventh straight weekly decline, after a report that the SEC is examining the company’s accounting. Nasdaq-100 futures were up about 6.6% and S&P 500 futures about 4.2% at 9:21 a.m. ET. Crypto stocks and miners jump Bitcoin-linked equities rallied with the chipmaker. item.title: UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues The U.K. will bar crypto exchange operators from trading against their own capital on the venues they run, while a new Treasury order clears independent market makers to trade on those platforms without a separate dealing permission. The Financial Conduct Authority’s final rules say a firm “must not execute any orders against its proprietary capital” on a qualifying trading platform it operates. The FCA’s guidance spells out the effect: a firm “cannot act as a market maker” on its own platform. The restriction takes effect Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA rule itself is not new. The regulator published it on June 30 in policy statement PS26/11, part of a five-document package that completed its crypto rulebook. What changed last week was the Treasury’s side of the framework. What the FCA rule covers The FCA’s rulebook defines a market maker as a person who holds themselves out on a platform on a continuous basis as willing to buy and sell qualifying cryptoassets against their own capital at prices they set. That is the activity operators will be barred from on their own venues. There is one carve-out. An operator with the appropriate permission may still engage in matched principal trading to execute client orders on its platform, as long as it follows the platform’s non-discretionary rules. The FCA warned that this model does not rule out settlement risk, so firms should take steps to minimize it. The bar applies only to the operator’s own platform. Under the same rules, an operator with the right permission can still trade against its own capital outside the venue it runs. It must make clear to clients which capacity it is acting in, and it must manage conflicts of interest. Treasury clears outside market makers The Treasury made the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2026 on Nov. 18. They add a new Article 9UA to the U.K.’s crypto legislation. The article carves two kinds of activity out of the regulated activity of dealing in qualifying cryptoassets as principal. One is activity carried on “otherwise than for the purpose of providing a service to another person.” The other is activity carried on “as a market maker on a qualifying cryptoasset trading platform.” In practice, a third-party firm quoting prices on a U.K. crypto platform would not need the principal-dealing permission for that activity. The text does not say who the market maker has to be, so the bar on operators comes from the FCA’s rules rather than from the Treasury order. The explanatory note says no impact assessment was prepared because no significant new costs are expected. The FCA’s rules also put new duties on platforms that rely on market makers. Operators must identify, document and monitor users running market-making strategies. If they offer incentive schemes or other arrangements to liquidity providers, they must document and disclose t

item.title: Everything going down at once wasn't evidence of a conspiracy – but the truth may be scarier
item.description: Have you or someone you love been affected by a tech outage this week? Yeah, us too. You can listen to the latest episode of The Kettle right here on this page, as well as on Spotify , Apple Music , or YouTube . Those platforms also let you subscribe to The Kettle, so you are always notified when the latest episode goes live In a week of big stories the biggest one seems to be the fact that everyone from Microsoft to the NSA was dealing with outages , and here's what might be the worst part: It doesn't seem to be AI, nor hostile countries intent on destroying our infrastructure. Unfortunately for all of us, what the past week of outages reveal is that – as we discussed on The Kettle less than a month ago – all of our essential tech infrastructure is basically held together with duct tape and twine. Join host Brandon Vigliarolo , cybersecurity editor Jessica Lyons , and open source reporter Liam Proven to discuss what comes next, and whether we can fix any of this without tearing all of it out and starting from scratch. A lightly edited transcript is included below: Brandon (00:04) Hi everyone and welcome to the latest episode of the Register's Kettle podcast. I'm your host, Reg reporter Brandon Vigliarolo, and if you're hearing this, then that means there isn't an outage right now, which seems like that might be a lot to ask of our technology in the past week. It's been a busy week. We had Anthropic's IPO , Nvidia drama continuing , and other stuff going on. But the one thing that everyone seems to be talking about is what's become known in the zeitgeist as Outagepalooza, as it seems like everything was offline at some point in the past few days. With me to discuss the chaos and the conspiracy theories they're giving rise to is Reg cybersecurity editor Jessica Lyons and our open source reporter Liam Proven. Guys, what's happening? Jessica Lyons (00:45) I've got my tinfoil hat on right now, so I'm ready. Brandon (00:48) Yes, I've had family calling me being like, my god, what's happening? Who's ending the world right now? Is it AI? Jessica Lyons (00:55) Ha ha ha. Brandon (00:56) We'll get to that part. Liam Proven (00:57) Wonderful. My mum's wardrobe door stuck this week and we found a company on the little rock in the middle of the Irish Sea that fixes sliding doors and he didn't get my emails because he's one hundred percent Microsoft and he uses Hotmail and it's Hotmail. Liam Proven (01:18) And when I got it through, you'd be amazed at the ramifications. I SMS'd him in the end and he got that and then was really angry because I said, "Dude, I've been trying to get you for three days. Can you at least reply and say Friday?" And he's like, "No, I've got no email, I've got no internet, I've got nothing." Brandon (01:32) My god. Yes, it's been an interesting week. So Jess, catch us up on everything that's fallen apart in the past few days. We've got quite a list growing here. Jessica Lyons (01:40) Yes. Well, we'll start with Outlook. I'm sorry, Mic

item.title: Strategy (MSTR) Adds 457 Bitcoin for $29.6 million
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy (MSTR) Adds 457 Bitcoin for $29.6 million Strategy (MSTR) bought 457 bitcoin last week for $29.6 million at an average of about $64,898 per coin, an 8-K filing shows, lifting its total to 851,305 BTC as the bitcoin price trades about under the company’s average cost. The purchase ran from Nov. 16 to Nov. 22. Strategy said it paid $64.23 billion for its stack, an average of $75,446 per coin including fees and expenses. That is $6 below the $75,452 average it reported a week earlier, so the new coins barely moved the cost basis. The buy is also smaller than the 485 bitcoin Strategy added the week before . Strategy shares were trading near $83.50 in premarket on Monday, up about 7% from Friday’s close near $78. How Strategy paid for the coins Strategy funded the purchase entirely with common stock. It sold 1,925,676 MSTR shares under its at-the-market program for net proceeds of $176.7 million, and no preferred stock was sold during the week. Only $29.6 million of that cash went into bitcoin. The rest went to buy back Strategy’s own STRC preferred stock, which is the pattern the company has followed for several weeks. Strategy repurchased 2,183,747 STRC shares for $211.8 million. It paid $147.0 million of that with MSTR proceeds and $64.8 million from its USD Cash balance. The preferred buyback was roughly seven times the bitcoin spend. The board also lifted the size of its digital credit securities repurchase program from $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion. After the increase, $1.12 billion remains available. About $17.9 billion of MSTR stock is still available under the ATM. The 457 coins were bought at an average of $64,898, which is above where bitcoin trades now. They also continue a slowdown: Strategy added 1,036 bitcoin in its Nov. 9 filing, 485 in its Nov. 16 filing and 457 in the latest one, while the preferred buybacks have grown. The stack equals about 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. Last week’s $29.6 million bitcoin spend was about 17% of the $176.7 million the ATM raised. Weekend low put Strategy deep under water Bitcoin hit a weekend low near $55,100, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. At that level, Strategy’s coins were worth about 27% less than the $75,446 it paid on average. The price has since recovered to around $61,000. At that level the 851,305 bitcoin are worth roughly $52 billion, about $12 billion below what Strategy paid. That is a paper loss only, since the filing shows no bitcoin sales during the week and the coins are still on the balance sheet. The slide has hit the stock hard. Strategy shares tumbled for a sixth straight day to about $86 on Thursday, and they fell again on Friday. A week ago the company said it was holding bitcoin modestly below cost , and the gap has widened since. Cash reserve moves to general use Strategy also changed how it labels its dollar cash.
